24. As may be seen from above, “in principle” approval given by this Department
under Centrally sponsored schemes of EI and ISC has been on the higher side, particularly during
2007-08 and this trend will be maintained in future also.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
25. The Committee notes the reply of the Department. Though the Department has
furnished the information on the number of projects approved/sanctioned for the last four
years but it has not furnished the information on the status of various ongoing projects
under these heads. The Committee desires to have the information on the status of various
road projects as these roads play a vital role in providing inter-State connectivity and also
link to cities which are economically important.
(Recommendation at Para 41)
26. The Committee is unhappy with the delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report on
Mughal Road in Jammu and Kashmir as a result of which, the competent authority could not
sanction the project. The Government, however, has not given any reason as to why there was
delay in finalizing the Detailed Project Report. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department to apprise the Committee about those reasons and action taken in the matter. The
Committee desires that the Department should fine tune its systems and procedures to avoid such
delays.
Reply of the Government
27. The 84 km long Mughal Road is to connect Shopian in Pulwama District of Kashmir Valley
with the remote areas of Poonch and Rajouri Districts of Jammu. The preliminary cost indicated
as approved in PM package was Rs.159.00 crore on the basis of feasibility report of 2001 and
reconnaissance survey conducted by M/s  RITES. The detailed survey and investigations of 84 km
road was required for preparation of Detailed Project Report. The stretch is in the remote areas
and terrain is hilly and difficult. The working period is very limited in the State of J&K due to
weather conditions. Further, this stretch is very near to the Pakistan border. Therefore, extra care

7
was required during survey due to security reasons. Therefore, submission of DPR has taken time
although Ministry has requested State PWD in July, 2006, September, 2007, November, 2007,
February, 2008 and March, 2008 for submission of Detailed Project Report. The DPR has now
been submitted by Government of J&K for an amount of Rs.638.85 crore in March, 2008. The
work is proposed to be considered under Economic Importance scheme. The Centre and State
shares are fifty percent each. The EFC procedure will be followed and CCEA clearance be obtained
for sanctioning of the project. The State Government has already awarded the work, which is
targeted to be completed by April, 2010.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
28. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that all out effort will be made to complete
the mughal road as per its schedule.
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS (ORIGINAL) WORKS — NH(O)
(Recommendation at Para 45)
29. The Committee is not happy with the mere 15.90% increase in allocation for the
maintenance of National Highways. The Committee was informed that an amount of Rs. 2280.00 crore
is required for maintenance and repair of roads annually, The Committee is of the opinion that
Government should give adequate importance for the maintenance and repair of non-NHDP
highways to ensure that investment made in the NHs does not go waste. The Committee
recommends that one-third of the cess collected for the financing NHDP projects should be
allocated for the maintenance and repair of highways. The Committee desires that the Department
should take up the issue with the Planning Commission for getting one third portion of the cess
collected for the maintenance and repair of National Highways as this non-NHDP National
Highways are considered as lifeline of Indian transport sector.
Reply of the Government
30. The matter regarding apportionment of one-third of the cess collected on fuel towards the
maintenance and repair of National Highways (non-NHDP highways) was taken up with Planning
Commission. Keeping in view that this may result in some investment gap in the NHDP funding,
the Planning Commission was requested to agree in-principle for allocating extra funds to meet this
gap. In a meeting held on 22nd April, 2008, a Committee headed by Shri Anwarul Hoda, Member,
Planning Commission has been constituted, to prepare a revised financing plan for the National
Highways Development Project (NHDP) involving the cess fund, duly keeping in view the fund
requirement for maintenance and repair of NHs.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
31. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and urges the Planning
Commission to take a view in this regard at the earliest.
DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS IN NORTH-EASTERN REGION
(Recommendation at Para 49)
32. The Committee notes that lot of programmes are on the anvil for the development of

8
National Highways in the North-East. The Committee hopes that the Department may be able to
utilize the entire allocated amount for the North-East.
Reply of the Government
33. Progress of works is reviewed from time to time and State Public Works Departments are
requested to expedite the expenditure so that the allocated amount is fully utilized.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
34. The Committee feels that progress of works in North-East should have been
furnished to the Committee. It, however, hopes that with the availability of sufficient funds
under this head, the executing agencies will be able to complete the projects under their
disposal in time.
CENTRAL ROAD FUND
(Recommendations at Para 54)
35. The Committee notes that the petrol pumps which are collecting the cess, hardly give any
bills for the purchase of petroleum products. In this way, the Committee apprehends that the
exchequer may be losing hundreds of crores of rupees as the exact amount collected may always
be under-reported. The Committee, therefore, recommends that it may be apprised about the
mechanism and procedure available for collection of cess towards Central Road Fund.
Reply of the Government
36. The matter relating to sale of petroleum products and the collection of cess etc. falls within
the purview of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. The matter has been taken up with that
Ministry for apprising the mechanism and procedure followed by them for collection of cess
towards Central Road Fund. The Committee will be apprised about this aspect on receipt of
comments from that Ministry.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
37. The Committee is at loss to see that the issue of under reporting of cess collected
on fuel has not received the importance that is deserved neither by the Department nor by
the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It is a very serious issue. The Department
should submit a note on this issue for its consideration within a month of the presentation
of the report.
Recommendation at Para 55
38. The Committee further notes that Railways is a profit-making Public Sector Enterprise. The
Committee could not, therefore, understand the rationale behind the pooling of a major chunk of
the Central Road Fund with the Railways. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Railways which itself capable to undertake developmental works, wherever required, may do so
from its own resources/profits instead of seeking allocation from the Central Road Fund.
Reply of the Government
39. Allocation of resources from the Central Road Fund for different purposes is governed by

9
the Section 10 of the Central Road Fund Act, 2000. According to Section 10 (1) (viii), the Central
Government is responsible for allocation of:
(a) fifty per cent of the cess on high speed diesel oil for the development of rural roads
in such manner as may be prescribed; and
(b) the balance amount of fifty per cent of cess on high speed diesel oil and the entire
cess collected on petrol as follows:
(i) an amount equal to fifty seven and one-half per cent of such sum for the
development and maintenance of National Highways;
(ii) an amount equal to twelve and one-half per cent for the construction of road
either under or over the railways by means of a bridge and erection of safety
works at unmanned, rail-road crossings; and
(iii) the balance thirty per cent on development and maintenance of roads other than
National Highways and out of this amount, ten per cent, i.e. three per cent of
the total share of State roads shall be kept as reserve by the Central Government
for allocation to States for implementation of State road schemes of Inter-State
and Economic Importance to be approved by the Central Government in terms
of clauses (iii) and (iv) of this section.
40. It may be observed from the above that the Railways are entitled to a specific amount from
the Central Road Fund for the construction of road either under or over Railways by means of
a bridge and erection of safety works at unmanned rail-road crossing. Since this is an allocation
governed by the statutory provision, the Railways cannot be denied of their share of the allocation
from the Central Road Fund.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
41. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and desires that the requisite
additional funds to the States from the CRF may be considered so that maintenance of
roads does not suffer.
ROAD SAFETY
(Recommendation at Para 64)
42. The Committee feels that school children are the best messiahs for preaching road
safety to their parents. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the road safety campaign
may give adequate importance to this aspect and the Department may rope in schools and
school children to spread awareness for road safety. The work done by the NGOs for raising
road safety awareness may also be given due publicity in media and local newspapers. This
may ensure the better functioning of NGOs and the public in general will keep watch on their
activities.
Reply of the Government
43. To inculcate the road safety habits amongst the school children, a scheme for setting up
Road Safety Clubs in school has been formulated and action for approval of the scheme by the
Planning Commission has been initiated. Apart from this, the quiz competition, essay competition,
drawing and painting competition are being sanctioned as activities for promoting road safety
awareness by NGOs on regular basis. The NGOs are to abide by the terms and conditions annexed

10
with the sanction letter as per which they have to give due publicity in the Press and other possible
media before starting the sanction activities. At the time of sanctioning grant to the NGOs for road
safety programme, a request is being made to the Transport Department of the concerned State
for strict monitoring of functioning of the NGOs.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
44. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hope that the Planning
Commission will give timely approval to the scheme of setting up Road Safety Clubs.
REFRESHER TRAINING OF DRIVERS IN UNORGANISED SECTOR AND HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
(Recommendation at Para 67)
45. The Committee feels that this is a welcome step. The Committee recommends that the
number of organizations sponsored by the Ministry is very low and insufficient compared to the
vastness of our transport sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government may
endeavour to finance at least one NGO in each of the districts of the country for imparting
refresher course to the drivers of Heavy Motor V ehicles. The Committee also recommends that a
proper monitoring mechanism may be put in place to ensure that the organizations are actually
imparting training to the drivers.
Reply of the Government
46. The number of drivers sanctioned under this scheme for imparting training is constantly
increasing. For the year 2008-09, the target fixed is 75000 drivers against 57850 drivers sanctioned
during 2007-08. However, due to fund constraint, it is not feasible to sanction grant to one NGO
in each district of the country. For proper monitoring of the implementation of the scheme, at the
time of sanction of grant to the NGO for imparting refresher training to the driver, Transport
Department of the concerned State Government is requested for proper monitoring. The second
and final installment is released to the NGO only after getting the Final Action Taken Report from
the concerned State.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
47. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and recommends that more funds
should be allocated for imparting training to drivers. Further, monitoring of NGOs by way
of obtaining utilisation certificates may be enforced.
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
(Recommendation at Para 70)
48. The Committee notes that the Planning Commission has discontinued the scheme of
Model Driving Training Schools. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the
discontinuance of the scheme. The Committee would also like to know whether any alternative
schemes are proposed by the Planning Commission to fill the gap of Model Driving Training
Schools.
Reply of the Government
49. Being a Centrally sponsored scheme, the Planning Commission has dropped the scheme of

11
Model Driver Training School. The revised scheme with certain changes for setting up Model
Driver Training School is being formulated and will be sent to the Planning Commission for their
approval shortly.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
50. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the revised scheme of
Model Driver Training School will be formulated on priority and the Committee may be appraised
about the new scheme once it is approved.
(Recommendation at Para 71)
51. The States where Model Driving Training Schools were sanctioned may be asked to
complete the projects in a time bound manner and funds may be allotted accordingly.
Reply of the Government
52. Out of 13, two schools have become operational. The financial assistance sanctioned to
schools in Assam, Karnataka, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchal, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa
and Nagaland has been released to them substantially and these schools are likely to be operational
very soon. A request to facilitate the progress of the sanctioned project for setting up of school
in Madhya Pradesh and Haryana are made on regular basis.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
53. The Committee recommends that all the 13 schools should be operational at the
earliest and other States may be persuaded to set up the schools.
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS ACCIDENT RELIEF SERVICE SCHEME
(Recommendation at Para 75)
54. The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department for providing trauma care.
At the very same time, the Committee feels that the present allocation of fund of Rs.2.20 crore
for the trauma care is too inadequate. The Government should try to augment the funding for
trauma care. The Committee is constrained to note the tardy progress made in purchasing cranes
and ambulances. The Committee also recommends that the formalities for purchasing cranes and
ambulances may be completed at the earliest so that the trauma care facilities can be put in place
without further delay.
Reply of the Government
55. The specifications for small size crane, 10-ton crane and ambulances have been reviewed
and order for procurement of 100 ambulances, 30 Nos. of 10-ton cranes and 19 small size
cranes have been placed during 2007-08 for the year 2008-09. The tender process for procurement
of 10-ton crane, small size crane and ambulances (to be provided by this Department to the
identified hospitals by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare) under this scheme has been
initiated.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
56. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

12
NATIONAL DATA BASE NETWORK
(Recommendation at Para 78)
57. Application of information technology for the development of the country is the mantra of
the day. Of course, the Department has taken initiatives in the right direction way back in the year
2001. The Committee notes that till now, only a few States have embarked on the course of
implementing IT enabled systems for driving licences and registration certificates. We have the
resources, talent and expertise in the IT field. The Committee wonders what prevent the
Government from implementing the IT-enabled systems in the Road Transport Sector. The
Committee notes that target for completion of the IT-enabled systems is 2009 which is not far
away. The Committee has doubt whether the Government will be able to meet the target which
they could not do for the last seven years. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matters
may be reviewed at the highest level and steps may be taken to remove the bottlenecks. The
Committee also recommends that those States which are not implementing the IT-enabled Driving
Licence (DL) and Registration Certificate (RC) may be persuaded highlighting the benefit and
importance of IT-enabled system for DL and RC. The Committee also recommends that some
incentive scheme may be developed in such a way that those States which are implementing the
IT enabled systems should get sanction for more projects and schemes.
Reply of the Government
58. For strengthening of National Database Network relating to Transport Sector, the matter is
being reviewed at the level of Secretary (RT&H) and Joint Secretary (Transport). For issue of
Smart Card based Driving License and Registration Certificate and to have their inter-operability
through out the country, meetings are being arranged with all the States/UTs to emphasize the need
for its early implementation and to discuss and eradicate the problems being faced by them.
Recently, an amount of Rs 299.50 lakh was released to NIC for the work of Data Migration to
National Standards in the Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) in the country to ensure that entire
data conforms to the National Standard. The project will be located at Delhi and data from 35
States/UTs will be brought on electronic media. This project will be completed within a period of
nine months. On 31-3-2008 the EFC meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Secretary
(RT&H) and the EFC proposal for creation of State Registers and National Register at a cost of
Rs.148.00 crore was approved.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
59. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the project will be
completed in time.
ROAD SAFETY EQUIPMENT AND POLLUTION TESTING AND CONTROL
(Recommendation at Para 81)
60. The Committee hopes that the steps taken by the Ministry will bear fruits in the near future.
The allocation of Rs.5.80 crore for the year 2008-09 is very meager compared to the vehicular
population of the country. The Committee recommends that more allocation need to be given to
the objectives of schemes so that the road safety and pollution control is achieved in its optimum
level.
Reply of the Government
61. Under this scheme, road safety equipments such as interceptors and pollution testing

13
equipments such as smoke meters and gas analysers are provided to the States/UTs for
enforcement of road safety laws and Pollution Under Control norms. The recommendation of the
Committee for enhanced allocation has been noted. It will be taken into consideration while
finalizing the BE for 2009-2010.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
62. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the Department
will give due importance to road safety equipments and pollution control instruments while
finalizing its BE for the year 2009-10.
NEW SCHEMES OF ELEVENTH PLAN
(Recommendation at Para 85)
63. The Committee welcomes the intention of the Government to set up more inspection and
maintenance centres to identify the vehicles which do not meet the emission and safety norms
subject to the condition that these new centres should not override the authority of State RTOs.
The Committee feels that some monitoring or regulatory authority should be put in place before
these centres become operational as there is a possibility that these centres can harass the vehicle
owners in connivance with the vehicle manufacturers to change their vehicles by citing one or
other reasons. The Committee also recommends that a proper mechanism should also be set up
to monitor the allocation is spent meaningfully.
Reply of the Government
64. The suggestion given by the Committee shall be kept in view while finalizing the proposal
for setting up of I & M Centres.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
65. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
NEW SCHEMES OF ELEVENTH PLAN
(Recommendation at Para 89)
66. The Committee is very much disappointed about the negligence on the part of the
Government in promoting public transport system in the country. The Committee is of the opinion
that cities are jammed with rising number of private vehicles and the villages are not even getting
adequate public transport facility. The Committee once again reiterates its earlier recommendation
that in the absence of user-friendly public transports, the people in the country are resorting to
excessive use of private vehicles and this has put the roads under undue pressure. The Committee
observes that most of the investment on roads is being extracted from the public itself but the
returns accruing to the users are not equitable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
efforts of the Government should focus on developing public transport, which discourages
excessive use of private vehicles. The Government should adopt a methodology, whereby, in the
more densely populated States, the rich and the affluent are asked to pay more for keeping more
than one vehicle.
Reply of the Government
67. Road Transport is a State subject. However, keeping in view the need for strengthening

14
public transport system in the country, an amount of Rs.24.99 crore has been kept for the year
2008-09 for providing financial assistance to the S tates/UTs to strengthen their public transport
system subject to the condition that the States are committed to take certain reform measures
required for the sector. A broad scheme in this regard is being formulated by this Department.
Earlier, the views of the Committee regarding differential taxes for the owners having more than
one vehicle have been brought to the notice of the States/UTs for necessary action at their end.
While finalizing the broad scheme for providing the financial assistance to the State,
recommendation of the Committee would be taken into account so that the States would have to
take such reform measures to avail financial assistance from Central Government.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
68. The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
CREATION OF NATIONAL ROAD SAFETY BOARD
(Recommendation at Para 92)
69. The Committee feels that the time has come for the creation of the much talked about
National Road Safety Board as the number of road accidents on national highways is increasing
in an alarming manner. The Committee recommends that the Department should pursue the matter
vigorously and take necessary actions to establish this Board at the earliest.
Reply of the Government
70. A Committee under the chairmanship of Shri S. Sundar, former Secretary, MOST was set
up in the year 2005 to deliberate and to make recommendations for creation of a dedicated body
on Road Safety and Traffic Management. The Committee submitted its report on 20-2-2007 inter-
alia recommending the creation of a National Road Safety and Traffic Management Board through
an Act of Parliament to oversee the road safety activities in the country. The Committee of
Secretaries (CoS) in its meeting held on 4-3-2008 has considered the proposal of this Department
for creation of the Board and has in-principle, accepted the same. As directed by the CoS, a note
for creation of the Board is being finalized for consideration of the Expenditure Finance Committee
(EFC). The EFC would look into the details of the Board including the mechanism of flow of funds
to the States/UTs from National Road Safety Fund.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
71. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and opines that the National Road
Safety and Traffic Management Board is the need of the hour and Department of Road
Transport is requested to pursue the case with the EFC and see that the formalities
regarding having such a Board are completed quickly.
TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
(Recommendation at Para 94)
72. The Committee once again recommends that once the capital and interest is recovered, the
users’ fee must be discontinued. The Committee is of the opinion that there is a need for
establishment of a regulator to determine the reasonable return to the investor on road projects
which is being considered as a yardstick for fixation of toll. The Committee appreciates that in
view of the resource crunch being faced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and

15
there is a genuine need for generation of additional revenue by the Ministry. Whenever any National
Highway is constructed, it leads to huge value addition to the land adjoining the National Highway
and these benefits of addition in value have so far been enjoyed by private agencies only. The
Government should also get advantage of the appreciation of land value because it is the taxpayer’s
money that has led to the value addition of that property. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government may explore the possibility of imposing some cess/tax on land adjoining
National Highways which is being utilized for commercial purpose on annual basis. This could
serve as a permanent source of income for the Government and the revenue so generated could
be ploughed back for the construction and maintenance of National Highways in the country.
Provision of ducting at the time of construction of National Highways for laying telephone and
electric cables also leads to value addition and can be explored for generating more funds for the
road sector. These measures may go a long way to meet the resource gap for maintenance and
construction of National Highways in the country.
Reply of the Government
73. The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee had made the same
recommendation while considering the Demands for Grants for the year 2004-05 of the Ministry
of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways. The recommendation was as follows:
“The Committee recommends that the Government may explore the possibility of imposing
some cess/tax on land adjoining National Highways, which is being utilized for commercial
purpose on annual basis. This could serve as a permanence source of income for the
Government and the revenue so generated could be ploughed back only for the construction
of National Highways in the country.”
74. The levy of cess/tax in respect of the indirect benefit like appreciation in land value due
to the coming of National infrastructure like National Highways in a nearby area is a complex issue
having legal and socio-economic implications. Considering the complexity of the issue, the above
recommendation was referred to the Ministry of Law and their advice was as follows:
(i) The land adjoining to National Highways in most cases will be agricultural or fallow
land. The power to levy taxes on such land and building is covered by the State list
and State Governments are only concerned.
(ii) The power to acquire land under the NH Act, 1956 is restricted and limited for
development, maintenance, management or operation of the National Highways.
Acquisition of land for the purpose of other activities is outside the scope of NH
Act, 1956. The land acquisition is to be done as per LA Act, 1894 if the intention is
to acquire land for construction of hotels and restaurants, etc. by the side of National
Highways.
(iii) The capital gain at the time of sale of adjoining land is taken as income for the
purposes of the Income Tax Act excluding agricultural income. Tax on capital gain is
already covered under the Income Tax Act.
75. In view of the above, it was decided not to take any further action on the recommendation
of the Committee.
76. As regards the recommendation of the Committee regarding discontinuation of the levy of
user fee, it is informed that the National Highways Act, 1956 provides for the levy of the user fee
(toll) for services or benefits referred in relation to the use of National Highway sections, bridges,
tunnels etc. The provision for discontinuation of levy of user fee was available in the National
Highways (Fees for the use of Permanent Bridges) Rules, 1992. These Rules were superseded at

16
the time of notification of the National Highways (Fees for the use of National Highway sections
and permanent bridges — Public Funded Project) Rules, 1997. According to Rule 11  of these
Rules, fee shall be collected in perpetuity by the executing agency. At present, there is no provision
for discontinuation of the fee in any of the user fee (toll) related Rules.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
77. The Committee notes the reply of the Department and desires to know the yardstick
with the Department for fixing the user fees on national highways. The Department is also
silent on the issue of creation of a revolving fund for financing of major road projects. The
Committee expects the Department to come out with some practical solutions to do away
with the user fee which is being imposed on the travelling public on the national highways.

17

REPORT
This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred Thirty-sixth Report on Demands for
Grants (2008-09) (Demand No.93) of the Ministry of Tourism, which was presented to the
Parliament on 28th April, 2008.
2. Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 27th August, 2008 in
respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been
categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 9, 23, 24, 51, 52, 54, 61, 68, 69, 75 and 76 Total-11
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Government replies:
Para No. 101 T otal-1
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have
not been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 14 and 22 T otal-2
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are
still awaited:
Para Nos. 30, 37, 38, 58, 64, 82, 83, 86, 92 and 97 Total-10
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of the action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry of Tourism. The recommendations
of the Committee contained in its One Hundred Thirty Sixth Report, action taken thereon by the
Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken
have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS AND ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2008-09
(Recommendation at Para 9)
5. The Committee observes that the Ministry of Tourism projected a requirement of
Rs.5405.58 crore (10% basis) and Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) for the entire Eleventh Plan
against this requirement, the Planning Commission approved an allocation of Rs.5156.00 crore for
carrying out major activities of the Ministry viz.  Augmentation of Tourist infrastructure,
Development of Human Resource for hospitality and travel trade, Promotion and Publicity, Creating
budget accommodation etc. The Committee also notes that in the Annual Plan 2008-09 the Ministry
has projected an outlay of Rs.1062.85 crore against which an amount of Rs.1000.00 crore was
allocated. The Committee deplores the tendency of Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance
for imposing cuts on the amounts demanded by the Ministry. This mismatch between projected
amount and sanctioned outlay may result in widening further the gap between the tourism potential

2
and development of tourism synergies for achieving the goals. The Committee feels that in order
to attain the National growth targets in the Eleventh Plan period, huge planned funding is required.
Thus, the Government spending for the Ministry of Tourism will have to be significantly stepped-
up from the present level to meet the investment targets. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should be provided with Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis)
by the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for the Eleventh Plan Period as per their
original demand. The Committees also recommends the Ministry of Tourism to take appropriate
caution and remedial action to absorb in time the allocation made to them.
Reply of the Government
6. The Ministry accepts the recommendation that Government spending on tourism needs to
be stepped up with increased plan outlay.
7. The views of the Hon’ble Committee has been conveyed to the Ministry of Finance and
Planning Commission for providing Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) as per original proposal for the
Eleventh Five Year Plan.
8. The Ministry is taking conscious efforts to incur evenly paced utilization, which was
evident in 2007-08 with Ministry achieving upto 42% in second quarter, 69% in third quarter and
99.86% by 31st March, 2008.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
9. The Committee notes that as per the recommendation of the Committee the Ministry
of Tourism has requested the Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission for providing
Rs.6569.61 crore (20% basis) as per original proposal for the Eleventh Five Year Plan. The
Committee again calls upon the Ministry to pursue with the Ministry of Finance and
Planning Commission for allocating the projected outlay. The Committee hopes that with
the allocation of the projected outlay for the Plan, the Ministry will be able to fully exploit
the tourism potentials besides developing tourist infrastructure in the country.
(Recommendation at Para 14)
10. The Committee notes that during 2007-08, the plan outlay of Rs.996.62 crore of Ministry
of Tourism was not subjected to any cut at RE stage. However, the Committee notes that during
the year 2007-08, out of the budgeted allocation of Rs.996.62 crore, the Ministry could spent
Rs.658.55 crore upto December, 2007 which clearly indicates the poor fiscal management in the
Ministry of Tourism. The Committee observes that the major portion of the budgetary outlays has
been utilized during the last quarter of the financial year. The Committee disapproves the tendency
of spending funds desperately towards the end of the financial year especially, in the months of
February and March. The Committee expects that the maximum amount of plan outlay would be
utilized suitably and substantially during the first two quarters of the financial year so that the
Ministry will be in a position to demand for higher allocations of the funds at RE stage for
implementation of various projects/schemes of augmentation of tourists infrastructure and
Promotion and publicity of tourism in the country. The Committee therefore, recommends the
Ministry to plan and incur their expenditure uniformly so that funds are utilized appropriately
throughout the year and the Ministry should shun the practice of incurring expenditure
indiscriminately towards the last quarter of the financial year. This way no alibi will be provided
to the Ministry of Finance to reduce the allocation at RE Stage. The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry should do away with procedural hurdles and maintain close liaison for the purpose
of review, monitoring, implementation and coordinating of projects/schemes to achieve the
envisaged targets.

11. The Ministry is taking special efforts for better fiscal management and as a result it has
been able to achieve evenly paced utilization of budget.
12. The Ministry of Tourism has been making efforts to incur the expenditure uniformly so that

(provisional) of the Plan allocation of Rs.953.00 crore with the pace of the expenditure evenly

in Ministry.
13. Constant efforts are also being made to strengthen the monitoring mechanism for early
implementation of projects to achieve the envisaged targets.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
14. The Committee notes the reply and desires to have the expenditure pattern of the
Ministry for the year 2007-08 and 2008-09 upto December, 2008 to ascertain the progress
of fiscal management, utilization of budgetary allocation and the details of the physical and
financial target set for achieving the progress. The Committee desires that for better
physical and financial monitoring of the projects sanctioned by the Ministry, proper
coordination with States/Union Territories may also be maintained through review meetings

AUGMENTATION OF TOURISM INFRASTRUCTURE
(Recommendation at Para 22)
15. The Committee notes that one of the reasons for underutilization of allocation is unspent
balances with the States and also non-submission of utilization certificates by most of the States
on time. The Committee observes that most of the time the Central Government delay in release
of funds to the State or releases it at the fag end of the financial year and expects the States to
utilize it in a very short time. The Committee criticizes this practice as obviously the States are
not in a position to spend the entire amount in such a short period and therefore have unspent
balance lying with them. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the release of the funds to
the States should be made on time so that they could utilize the amount rationally under proper
monitoring of expenditure. The Committee also desires that there should be proper coordination
with the State Government, so as to obtain utilization certificates and to safeguard that money
released is spent only on approved infrastructure development projects.
Reply of the Government
16. The Ministry of Tourism has planned and incurred the expenditure uniformly so that funds
are utilized appropriately throughout the year. The funds are released to the State Governments
based on their project proposals which are complete as per the scheme guidelines. It is further
submitted that the Ministry released funds to State Governments/Union Territories for infrastructure
projects which have implementation schedule of 2-3 years. To avoid the accumulation of unspent
balance with the States, the Ministry of Tourism releases the 2nd instalment only when the UC for
the 1st instalment is received. For better physical and financial monitoring of the projects
sanctioned by the Ministry, proper coordination with States/Union Territories is also being
maintained through review meetings and site visits from time to time.

4
17. In the year 2007-08, the Ministry of Tourism released 70% of available budget for
infrastructure development by the end of September and 100% by the end of December to allow
sufficient time to State Governments to start the implementation of the projects.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
18. The Committee feels that waiting unduly long for utilization certificates would
unnecessarily delay the infrastructure projects and thereby creation of assets for tourism
infrastructure development. The Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry to evolve
a more efficient mechanism for the utilization of funds and obtaining the Utilization
Certificate. The Committee further recommends that proper coordination with States/Union
territories should also be maintained for the purpose.
(Recommendation at Para 23)
19. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts to develop quality
tourism infrastructure at major tourist destinations and circuits for developing tourist products and
providing better services to both domestic and international tourists. The Committee observes that
tourism is one of the economic sectors in the country that has the potential to grow at high rate
and can ensure consequential development of the infrastructure of the destinations and circuits. The
Committee feels that the infrastructure development holds the key to India’s sustain growth in the
tourism sector, therefore, tourist sites and destinations needs to be carefully selected on the basis
of their potential to provide all infrastructural facilities required by the tourists within such
destinations and circuits. The Committee is of the opinion that, if, India has to exploit its vast
inherent potential in tourism, then it must provide exclusive quality tourism product and destinations
comparable with other Asian countries like Singapore, Malaysia, Maldives, Thailand and China. As
tourism cannot develop independent of other infrastructure, therefore, a lot of information
dissemination is required in addition to hospitality and the scope and reach of the domestic tourism
should also be broadened through development of these competitive destinations and circuits. The
Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to develop quality tourism at identified tourist
circuits and destinations with focus on mega destinations and circuits that match international
standards and satisfy the domestic and international tourists. The aggressive marketing and publicity
of these destinations and circuits should also be done to generate a niche market of Indian tourism
products. The Committee also urges the Ministry that while selecting a destination or a circuit they
should attach priority for harmonious growth and development of all the Regions and States.
Reply of the Government
20. The mega destinations/circuits have been identified in consultation with the State
Governments on the basis of data indicating foot falls, and potential arrivals for creation of world
class infrastructure in all regions of country. The Ministry is working with other Central
Government Ministries and concerned State Governments to achieve convergence and synergy with
other Government programmes so that the impact of investment in these destinations and circuits
is maximized. The Ministry of Tourism has also taken up issues related to air, rail and road
connectivity with the concerned Ministries for holistic development of these destinations/circuits.
21. Developed destinations/circuits are also being promoted in domestic and overseas markets.
(Recommendation at Para 24)
22. The Committee also recommends that in order to maximize the impact of investment on
tourism infrastructure, the Ministry should make efforts for convergence of these mega destinations

5
and circuits and projects with Jawahar Lal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for
integrated development of infrastructure services, urban renewal, asset management and urban
governance.
Reply of the Government
23. The Ministry of Tourism has already made efforts for convergence of mega destinations
and circuits which are covered under Jawahar Lal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM) for their holistic and integrated development. Convergence of the resources is being
ensured so that the tourism related infrastructure and urban civic infrastructure complement each
other.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
24. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is making efforts with the State
Government to identify the sites/location for the development of mega destination and
circuits. The Committee also notes that the Ministry was making efforts for better
coordination and convergence of the resources with other Government schemes so as to
increase the flow of investment in these mega circuits/destination. The Committee feels
that a more consistent and proactive approach in vigorous marketing of product needed to
provide quality tourism infrastructure in the country. We would have to gives added impetus
to this effort which is yet to show the desired impact. The Committee recommends the
Ministry to pursue the matter with other Ministries and the State Governments in this
regard.
RURAL TOURISM
(Recommendation at Para 30)
25. The Committee notes that the rural tourism projects promoted under the scheme for
Product/Infrastructure Development of Destinations/Circuits targets rural artisans, artists and
service providers as primary beneficiaries for increase of tourist traffic to these rural destinations.
The Committee is of the view that Rural Tourism has great potential and prospects in the country
as it helps to provide boost to local performing arts and help conserve the local culture apart from
preventing rural urban migration. The Committee feels that the Rural Tourism needs to be given
impetus by allocating funds for the Rural Tourism projects for each State and the villages should
be identified for priority development involving the local bodies in the management. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Ministry to focus development of rural tourism infrastructure involving
local community in order to promote tourism in rural area and percolate its socio-economic benefit
there.
Reply of the Government
26. So far Ministry of Tourism sanctioned 128 rural tourism sites in 27 States.
27. In order to ensure that the socio-economic benefits of tourism percolate down to the rural
communities, Rural Tourism projects have focussed on boosting livelihood and preserving traditional
craft. The emphasis is on the site artisans structured involvement, progressing from national to
regional and international levels at Dilli Haat, the India International Trade Fair, the Toshali Mela
in Bhubaneshwar and at the India@60 roadshow in Singapore. Several sites such as Hodka in
Gujarat, Aranmula in Kerala, Nagger in H.P., Hee-Bermoik in Sikkim are proving to be successful
models of income generation, cultural preservation and gender empowerment.

6
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
28. The Committee feels that the number of sanctioned 128 rural tourism sites in 27
States is very less that needs to be increased to cover all the States/U.Ts. Besides, the status

SHORTAGE OF ACCOMMODATION
(Recommendation at Para 37)
29. The Committee notes that to meet the shortage of about 40,000 rooms during the
Commonwealth Games 2010 in Delhi and NCR, the Ministry has mooted a proposal to Central and
State Governments for augmenting the accommodation infrastructure for growth and quality of the
tourist facilities and to create infrastructure by converting selected Government properties into
heritage hotels and making use of the vacant land in Government premises including surplus land
available with the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Railways and D.D.A. for creation of land banks and
development of hotels sites on revenue sharing basis and granting extra FSI/FAR for hotels. The
Committee also notes that a capital and interest subsidy schemes for accommodation infrastructure
upto 3 star and heritage basic hotels and a tax holiday for five years to budget and upto 4 star
category hotels have been introduced as a incentive to combat crisis besides finalization of
guidelines for the home stay programme under “Incredible India Bed and Breakfast Scheme”. The
Committee observes that there is a steep escalation for room tariffs in India which is an indication
of increasing demand for tourist accommodation. The committee feels that if such a condition
prolongs, the tourists being priced out and may opt for an alternative destination in another country.
The Committee is of the view that the migration of the tourist might have long-term implications
in terms of potential loss of future stream of tourists in favour of competing tourist destinations.
The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to explore the possibility of construction of
hotels on surplus land with Airports Authority of India and Ministry of Railways to meet the
demand for additional rooms in the wake of the Commonwealth Games 2010. The Committee also
urges the ministry to impress upon the Central and States Governments for implementation of
single window clearance system for tourism projects in order to encourage the private players to
build hotels in the country. This would not only optimize the utilization of infrastructure facilities
but also make the future investment viable.

Tourism has through its Task Force meetings on creation of additional accommodation for the

to explore the possibility of construction of hotels in their surplus land. So far fourteen Task Force
meetings have been held. This Ministry is also in constant touch with the States of Uttar Pradesh
and Haryana for the identification of additional hotel sites.

RELAXATION OF THE RESTRICTED AREA PERMIT (RAP)/PROTECTED AREA PERMIT
(PAP)/INNER LINE PERMIT (ILP) REGIME
(Recommendation at Para 64)
50. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is in constant touch with Ministry of
Home Affairs to relax/abolish the requirement of permit system in the country as the growth of
international tourism is based on development of tourism in that destination. The Committee is of
the view that foreign tourists constitute an important component of tourists who wish to visit the
country specially the North Eastern States and Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands.
The restrictions on foreigners to stay beyond permitted period and visiting only selected islands/
regions/destination has discouraged the foreign tourists arrival in the country. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that in order to optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these islands/
regions/destinations, the restrictions on the foreigners on visiting the islands/regions may be
removed and they may be permitted to stay/ enjoy the beauty of the islands/regions/destination for
a longer periods. The Committee also feels that opening up new islands/regions/destination for
foreigners also needs to be given priority. The Committee recommends the Ministry of Tourism to
vigorously pursue the matter of review of liberalization of the entire RAP/P AP/ILP regime at the
highest level in the Ministry of Home Affairs which act as a hindrance to the growth and
development of domestic and international tourism to those regions. The Committee may be
apprised of the outcome in the matter from time to time.
Reply of the Government
51. In order to boost tourism in these areas, the issues for which relaxation/abolition of the
RAP/PAP regime, is being sought, are:
• Tourists desirous of visiting areas having the RAP/PAP regime are required to travel in
a group of minimum of 4. Some of the places also require that they should be
accompanied by a liaison officer. In fact several areas such as Nanda Devi in
Uttarakhand and some areas of Sikkim do not permit individual tourists. The requirement
should be removed as the trend today is increasingly towards individual tourists.
• The maximum number of days that the tourist is permitted to stay at these places is
also restricted to 7, 10 or 15 days (only exception are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
where they are permitted 45 days). This restriction should be removed so that tourists
can visit these areas at leisure.
• The routes for regions covered by RAP/PAP regime are also delineated by the Ministry
of Home Affairs due to which the tourists are restricted from visiting other interesting
places which may fall off these routes. This restriction should also be removed.
• Some of these States mentioned above even have an Inner Line Permit which has to
be taken by the domestic tourists visiting these areas. There is an urgent need to
completely relax/withdraw this permit as growth of international tourism to a region is
based on development of tourism in that destination.

and circuits including cultural heritage sites. (Para 74)
The Committee notes that as per its recommendation, the Ministry of Tourism has
taken up the issues related to improvement of road, rail and air connectivity with the
Ministries of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, Railways and Civil Aviation and
Planning Commission. The Committee also notes that an Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG)
has been constituted under Committee on Infrastructure to look into the issues of
connectivity for the growth of tourism in the country. The Committee recommends the
Ministry to impress upon the IMG to come out with a perspective plan for proper
connectivity of places of tourist interest across the country so as to encourage the visit
of the tourist to such places. (Para 77)
MULTICIPLICTY OF TAXES
The Committee notes that Ministry of Tourism has taken up the issue of
rationalization of Luxury Tax in hotels and V AT on food and beverages and sales tax or
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) and the high rate of taxation on tourist transport vehicles
with Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers through Ministry of Finance. The
Committee recommends the Ministry to try to evolve consensus on the subject in order
to give a further boost to tourism and promote India as a “Value for Money” destination.
(Para 82)
VISA ON ARRIVAL SCHEME
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has mooted a proposal of
granting visa-on-arrival scheme for 18 designated countries and a Committee of
Secretaries (CoS) note to the concerned Ministries on the issue of ‘Visa-on-Arrival’ and
‘Long Term Visa’ has already been circulated. The Committee feels that with the
liberalization of visa regime and introduction of multiple entry long term tourist visas for
tourists and implementation of APIS would facilitate tourist arrivals in the country and
increase India's share internationally. The Committee recommends the Ministry to

24
impress upon all concerned Ministries for expediting the issue of ‘Visa-on-Arrival’ and
‘Long Term Visa’ facilities under intimation to the Committee. (Para 85)
SPECIAL TOURISM POLICE
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism is consistently following up the
State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for deploying tourist police in
their States at important tourist centres for safety and security of tourists and a guideline
have been formulated in consultation with Ministry of Home, Ministry of Defence to form
Tourist Security Organisation deploying primarily Ex-Servicemen. The Committee
recommends the Ministry to persuade the remaining States for the formation of tourism
police force for ensuring safety and security of the tourists and to curb the rising
incidents of cheating, fleecing criminal acts and harassment of foreign tourists including
gender abuse. (Para 88)
COORDINATION WITH V ARIOUS DEPARTMENTS
The Committee notes the Empowered Sub-Committee of the Committee on
Infrastructure is looking into the issues affecting the growth of tourism in the country
and effecting co-ordination and making decision on the policy matter amongst various
Ministries. The Committee however, recommends the Ministry of Tourism to make some
institutional arrangement within the Ministry at apex level for better co-ordination and
inter-face with other Ministries/Department for development and promotion of tourism in
the country. (Para 91)

25

VIII

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture, having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Forty Sixth Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the
Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Thirty Seventh
Report on Demands for Grants 2008-09 of the Ministry of Culture”.
2. The One Hundred and Thirty Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the
28th April, 2008.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained on its
One Hundred and Thirty Seventh Report were received from the Ministry of Culture on the
5th September, 2008.
6. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the
18th December, 2008.
SITARAM YECHURY
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
December 18, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Agrahayana 27, 1930  (Saka) Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture.

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Thirty-seventh Report on
Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Culture, which was presented to the
Parliament on 28th April, 2008.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 5th September, 2008 in
respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. The Replies have been
categorized as follows:—
Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 13, 14, 16, 19, 24, 26, 27, 29, 30, 34, 37, 40, 43, 49,
51, 54, 58, 61, 62, 65, 67, 70, 76, 80, 83, 86, 89, 91, 94, 95,
101, 105, 108, 113, 115, 119, 125, 126, 127, 129
Total–40
Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been
accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. T otal–Nil
Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited:
Para Nos. 8, 12, 21, 32, 46, 73, 111 Total–7
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of the action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the
Committee contained in the One Hundred and Twentieth, action taken thereon by the Government
and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken have been given
in the succeeding paragraphs.
Budget allocation and overall assessment of the financial performance for the year 2007-08
(Recommendation at Para 8)
5. The Committee notes that the expenditure trend during 2007-08 is not very satisfactory.
For the plan allocation, expenditure of Rs.370.39 crore has been incurred out of the RE of
Rs.520.00 crore. In the non-plan also, expenditure of Rs.298.00 crore has been incurred out of
Rs.460.00 crore upto 29th February, 2008. Thus, Rs.149.61 crore in plan and Rs.161.28 crore in
non-plan remained to be utilized in the month of March, 2008.
Reply of the Government
6. As against Rs.520.00 crore of RE, under Plan an expenditure of Rs.470.46 crore was incurred
upto 31st March, 2008 which constitutes 90.47% of RE. Under Non-Plan, an expenditure of
Rs.394.03 crore was incurred upto 31st March, 2008 which constitutes 85.66% of RE-2007-08.

2
Statements indicating organization/scheme-wise break up of actual expenditure under Plan and Non-
Plan Heads for 2007-08 are attached at Annexure ‘A’ and ‘B’.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
7. The Committee notes that the total expenditure incurred was 90.47% in plan and
85.66% in non-plan of RE allocation in the year 2007-08. It, however, emphasises the need
for achieving total utilization of funds every year.
(Recommendation at Para 12)
8. The Committee is unhappy to note that despite its concern and considered recommendation,
the Ministry of Finance has refused to review the budgetary allocations in the month of December
instead of in the month of September thereby subjecting the Ministry of Culture to financial cuts
at RE stage. The Committee observes that there is a greater need and scope for scrutiny of entire
exercise of budgetary process beginning from budgetary proposals in September by the Ministry
of Finance in respect of Ministry of Culture because of its special needs. The Committee feel that
the entire budgetary process and procedure involving about eight months has actually given both
to the evil of mis-utilisation of funds in a hurried manner and apprehension of losing valuable but
scarce financial resources made available to them by Ministry of Finance at the fag end of the
financial year. It appears that given the rigidity in budgetary exercise the Ministry of Finance has
failed to assess actual requirements of the Ministry of Culture for funds to be utilized for various
developmental purposes. The Committee is of the firm belief that the under utilization to a great
extent in the Ministry of Culture is the result of rigid financial practices and procedures. The
Committee therefore, recommends the Planning commission and Ministry of Finance for giving an
active consideration through a rigorous and rational scrutiny for reforming and rescheduling of the
present Budgetary procedures and practice as far the Ministry of Culture is concerned, so that the
final plan and non-plan allocations are conveyed to the Ministry and to respective institutions/
organizations by the month of December every year for effective and fruitful utilization of scarce
financial resources. Alternatively, the Committee recommends that the possibility may be explored
for provision of budget allocations for various activities may be converted as non-lapsable fund
taking into account the seasonal nature of work and activities undertaken by various institutions
under the Ministry of Culture.
Reply of the Government
9. The above recommendation was sent to Ministry of Finance (MoF) and Planning
Commission for their consideration. Planning Commission held a meeting on 9.07.2008 with
Ministry of Culture to discuss the above issue and decided that they would take up the matter with
MoF for a more empathetic view while reviewing the budget of the MoC at RE stage. A response
has also been received from MoF but they have expressed their inability to agree to the proposal.
The matter will be once again taken up with them during pre-budget discussions.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
10. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and wishes to know the reasons
Ministry of Finance has given for not agreeing to its proposal. The Committee further
recommends that the Ministry of Culture may pursue the matter with the Ministry of
Finance again and present the case of the Ministry of Culture in an effective way indicating
special nature of requirements and seasonal activities undertaken by various organizations
of Ministry of Culture.

3
(Recommendation at Para 13)
11. The Committee is happy to note that for the first time, allocation for the Ministry of Culture
has reached to four figures. The Committee feels that it is a good beginning for this vital sector
which has huge potential but yet to be explored. The Committee hopes that all the new schemes
and projects taken up by the Ministry during the financial year 2008-09 will be completed in a time
bound manner.
Reply of the Government
12. All Divisional Heads have been instructed for taking necessary action to follow up the
implementation of new schemes. Two new plan schemes have been launched and other schemes
are under various stages of approval. All efforts are being made to streamline the process, so as
to hasten the pace of various approvals. Regular reviews have been initiated which are expected
to yield the desired results.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
13. The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the Ministry and desires to know that
new plan schemes launched by the Ministry of Culture. The Ministry should also endeavour
to launch all the schemes as soon as they are approved.
(Recommendation at Para 14)
14. The Committee also recommends that possibility of organizing off-season festivals and
organizing Dance/Cultural Programmes throughout the year may be explored. The Ministry should
also explore for decentralization of some of the schemes which can help the Zonal Centres in
expediting their work. This will certainly help in providing much needed relief to the Ministry. The
Committee also recommends that in spite of the constraints faced by the Ministry, there is need
to spread the expenditure evenly and making efforts for full utilization of the allocated amount
through proper planning and monitoring. Only then the desired result for Eleventh Five year Plan
can be achieved.
Reply of the Government
15. Recommendation of the Committee has been noted for guidance. Efforts are being made to
convene the meeting of Expert Committees for selection of beneficiaries under various schemes of
the Ministry more often rather than once a year to ensure even spread of expenditure and to
encourage organizations to hold off-season festivals/dance/cultural programmes. A decision has also
been taken to decentralize schemes relating to Performing Arts and seminars/workshops on culture
and to implement them through Zonal Cultural Centres. Further necessary action is being taken for
seeking EFC/SFC approval etc.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
16. The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the Ministry and hopes that the
intended objectives could be achieved only by proper planning, effective and close
monitoring and judicious utilization of resources.
(Recommendation at Para 16)
17. The Committee notes the efforts made by the Ministry to improve its performance. The
Committee may be apprised of the findings of the three members Committee and the steps

4
proposed to be taken to improve the performance of various schemes being implemented by the
Ministry of Culture.
Reply of the Government
18. A Committee comprising Shri Bhaskar Ghose (Former Secretary, Culture), Shrimati Shovana
Narayan and Shri R. C. Mishra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture was set up by the Ministry
of Culture to examine and review various schemes of the Ministry and make recommendations for
their modification and changes in the mode of their implementation. The Committee after detailed
deliberation has submitted its report which inter alia proposes higher awards/grants to beneficiaries
and greater decentralization in the process of selection. Steps are being taken to take SFC/EFC
approvals to carry out necessary changes in the relevant schemes.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
19. The Committee appreciates the efforts made by the Ministry to get its schemes
examined and reviewed by an expert Committee. It hopes that the Ministry will take all the
approvals etc. well in time so that the recommendation of the Ghose Committee are
implemented without losing time.
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)
(Recommendation at Para 19)
20. The Committee notes that the cases of vanishing of our monuments is a dangerous process
which if not controlled in time, may lead to a situation where we will be left with only a few
monuments as symbols of our culture and tradition. The vanishing of monuments should be
stopped with all the resources at our disposal. The Committee notes that the Ministry has already
taken appropriate measures to prevent it. The Committee may be apprised about the findings of the
internal Committee to study the problems and the steps taken to implement the findings with the
result it achieved.
Reply of the Government
21. Directions have been issued to all the Circles of the Archaeological Survey of India to
arrange inspection of the monuments under their jurisdiction at ‘least three times a year’ by the
officers including the Head of the Circle i.e. Superintending Archaeologist to assess the status of
the monument, state of conservation, maintenance, encroachments and misuse (if any), available
tourist amenities, further upgradation, status of watch and ward arrangements, etc.
22. The Chairman of the in-house Committee of officers in the ASI has sought the old records,
photographs and drawings, copies of the protection notifications, details on the last inspection
done, ASI officials posted last, land revenue details, possible reasons for disappearance, published
data, since when not traceable and other relevant data from the Circles in respect of the
untraceable monuments for detailed examination by the Committee at the end of July, 2008. A
search of the old records pertaining to untraceable monuments is also being carried out in the
archives of the Directorate General.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
23. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry. It would like to have inspection
reports submitted by Delhi Circle made during 2007 and 2008. However, it is not satisfied
with the efforts made for controlling the cases of vanishing of monuments. Everyday more

5
news about the vanishing of monuments appears. The Ministry has to take stern action
against the culprits and sensitize the police Department also so that the things may be
taken care at the initial stage itself. The Ministry should also make more documentaries/
Ads and make common man aware of our heritage. A centralized Cell should also be created
where people can make complaints in case they see any encroachment. The Committee
further recommends that the Government should undertake a survey and enlist all the
existing monuments in the country which are not in the list of ASI and State Government
but need protection as heritage.
(Recommendation at Para 21)
24. The Committee hopes that ASI will learn from its past experience on the reasons for under-
utilizations of allocated funds and take appropriate steps to utilize the allocated resources. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry should take immediate steps to operationalise National
Mission on Monuments and Antiquities and expedite formation of State level implementation
committees so that funds are utilized within the financial year. The Committee may be apprised
about the steps taken to operationalise NMMA and the status of its implementation.
Reply of the Government
25. With a view to operationalise National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities, State
Level Implementation Committees comprising ex-officio  members and experts (including those
suggested by the State Governments) have already been constituted in 15 States. These are:
Assam, Bihar, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka,
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Tripura and West Bengal. The
National Mission will soon initiate action to take up various activities in these States as per its
mandate.
26. In the Second Meeting of the Monitoring Committee for the National Mission on
Monuments and Antiquities held on 13th June, 2008 it has been decided to form a Sub-Committee
under the chairmanship of DG, ASI, to consider and recommend changes in the structure of the
National Mission to streamline its functioning and ease the distribution/allocation of funds to the
States for undertaking various projects/programmes of the Mission in the States/UTs.
27. The work of compilation of village-wise data on unprotected built heritage and sites from
secondary sources is already in progress. Data pertaining to more than 15000 villages has been
compiled in the prescribed template so far. The National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities has
initiated planning for conduct of training workshops on capacity building, awareness generation,
and heritage outreach programmes.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
28. The Committee also desires that the work of the sub-Committee should be completed
in a time bound manner so that the problem of non-utilization of funds does not arise. The
Committee notes that State Level Implementation Committees have been constituted in 15
States, where the National Mission can take up its activities. The Committee hopes that
implementation Committee will soon be constituted in the remaining States also. The
Committee notes there is substantial progress in compilation of village-wise data on
unprotected built heritage. However, the Committee feels that vigorous efforts are required
to cover the entire nation. The National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities is a long
awaited mission and the Ministry should make all out efforts to attain the objectives of
mission, in time.

6
(Recommendation at Para 24)
29. The Committee notes that more than 56 excavation reports are pending with ASI since
2002. The Committee is of the view that this is a serious matter since there is inordinate delay
in the preparation of reports. The Committee hopes that with the new system in place, there will
be no delay in preparation of reports on excavation in future.
Reply of the Government
30. Out of the 56 pending reports with ASI, 19 excavation reports have been received. These
are: (i) Udaigiri, (ii) Lal Kot, (iii) Hathab, (iv) Thakurani Tila, (v) Shyam Sundar Tila,
(vi) Mahabalipuram, (vii) Lachchura, (viii) Ojiyana, (ix) Kanaganahalli, (x) Besnagar, (xi) Bhita
(xii) Chandor, (xiii) Bekal Fort, (xiv) Boxanagar, (xv) Golbai Sasan, (xvi) Satdhara, (xvii) Birchhabili
Tila, (xviii) Tamluk, and (xix) Khajuraho. Besides 2 part reports on (i) Dholavira and (ii) Sravasti
excavations, have been submitted.
31. The Archaeological Survey of India has taken necessary steps to clear the pendency in the
excavation reports of ASI as well as other research institutions like Universities, State Departments
of Archaeology etc. The revised format for inviting proposals in this regard clearly specifies that
unless reports on previous excavations are submitted, further approvals shall not be granted. The
ASI has also requested all agencies undertaking excavations to clear all the pending reports on the
excavations carried out in the past and is monitoring the progress in this regard.
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
32. The Committee feels that efforts made by ASI in expediting the reports need further
impetus. ASI should continue to make vigorous monitoring in proactive manner to get the
reports in time bound manner.
(Recommendation at Paras 26 and 27)
33. The Committee notes the steps taken by the Ministry to prevent encroachments. The
Committee desires that possibility of making financial provision to pay for the rehabilitation of the
encroachers who are removed from monuments may also be explored in consultation with Ministry
of Finance so that the Ministry is not dependent on respective State Government for rehabilitation
of encroachers.
34. The Committee also notes that more than 249 centrally protected monuments have been
encroached upon by various elements due to multifarious reasons. Some of the reasons are
historical whereas some others are socio-economic in nature. The Committee observes that the
problem needs to be addressed on a permanent basis with a lasting solution wherever possible.
Appropriate mechanisms may be evolved to rehabilitate the encroachers and the Government should
ensure the retrieved monuments are not illegally occupied again. The Committee notes that an
appropriate Committee may be constituted to look into the various aspects of the encroachments
with the mandate to recommend appropriate mechanism for finding a solution. This may be done
on a time bound basis.
Reply of the Government
35. In accordance with the recommendations of the Committee, the Circles of the
Archaeological Survey of India have been issued directions to closely liaise with the State
Governments and local administrations to remove the encroachments. In fact, in some States, a
Committee has also been constituted for encroachment removal from the monuments. To cite an

7
example, in Delhi, a Committee under the Chairmanship of the Divisional Commissioner of the
Government of NCT, Delhi with Superintending Archaeologist as Member Secretary and NDMC,
MCD, Delhi Cantonment Board, DDA, Revenue, Police and Delhi Wakf Board as members is in
place.
36. The Archaeological Survey of India is in the process of formulating a policy for
rehabilitation of the encroachers. The concerned Circles have been asked to procure details of the
rehabilitation policies of the respective State Governments and work out the details for the
rehabilitation of encroachers at each monument including the total amount the Archaeological
Survey of India will have to pay to the State Government/encroachers.
37. Even without a formal rehabilitation policy in place, a few monuments in Delhi, like Nila
Gumbad (behind Humayun’s Tomb), Red Fort, Bade Khan and Chhotey Khan Tombs have been
freed of encroachments. Similarly, Bangalore Circle in collaboration with the Government of
Karnataka has finalized a proposal to rehabilitate 35 encroachers from the protected area of
Chitradurga Fort by agreeing to pay 50% of the amount likely to be spent.
38. Archaeological Survey of India has also taken a decision to adequately fence and properly
guard all centrally protected monuments in a phased manner. The Circles have also been directed
to fence and landscape the protected area immediately after the encroachments are removed so that
recurrence of encroachments is ruled out. The Circles have also been directed to strengthen the
watch and ward arrangements at the monuments that are prone to encroachment.
39. Although State level and District level Committees do exist in some States, the Circles have
been asked to approach the concerned State Government authorities to get a Committee of officers
of the concerned Government Departments constituted to deal with the problem of encroachments
in protected monuments/sites.
40. The Superintending Archaeologists of Circles are vested with the powers of Estate Officer
to issue eviction notices/orders to the encroachers under the Public Premises (Eviction of
Unauthorized occupants) Act, 1971. They are also authorized to issue show cause notices under
the provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 and
Rules, 1959.
41. As and when encroachment is noticed/reported in the protected area, the Superintending
Archaeologist issues notice to the encroacher under section 19 of the Ancient Monuments,
Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 for removal of unauthorized buildings. Simultaneously
help from the local police is sought by lodging a complaint and by registering FIR.
42. On receipt of a report from the field office, the Director General, Archaeological Survey
of India, issues demolition orders to the offender in pursuance of Section 19 (1) of the Ancient
Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 for removal of such encroachments/
unauthorized construction within a specified period. A copy of the order issued by the Director
General is also sent to the District Collector. In case the person to whom demolition order has been
issued refuses or fails to comply, the Director General directs the District Collector to cause the
unauthorized building removed as per Section 19 (2). The help and assistance in removal of
encroachments is also sought from the respective State Government where there are no fruitful
results, action is initiated against the encroachers by filing cases in the courts of law.

8
then we have such a large number of encroachments on our protected sites? The

in the regard.

steps like generating awareness towards protection and maintenance of beauty of the Monuments
as valuable national heritage.

awareness among the population about bad effects of defacement of monuments is giving an
impetus to the tourism sector. The Committee feels, the propaganda mechanism needs to be more

defacement of our monuments. Moreover, the Committee notes that a special campaign may be
launched to educate the school children for the preservation of our monuments. In addition to this,
