INTRODUCTION  
  I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary  Standing Committee on, Transport, Tourism and Cult ure, 
having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this One Hundred a nd Fifty Third 
Report on Action Taken by the Government on the Rec ommendations/Observations of the Committtee contained in its 
One Hundred and Forty Ninth Report on Development of Tourism Infrastructure and Amenities for the Commonwealth 
Games 2010. 
2.  The One Hundred and Forty Ninth Report of the D epartment-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the 24 
th  February, 2008. 
3.  The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations  of the Committee contained on its One Hundred and Forty 
Ninth Report were received from the (i) Ministry of Tourism on the 17 th  August 2009; (ii) Ministry of Civil Aviation on 
the 24 th  August 2009; (iii) Ministry of Urban Development on the 26th August 2009; (iv) Government of NCT of D elhi 
on the 6 th  January, 2010; and (v) Ministry of Culture on 4 th  February, 2010. 
4.  The Committee considered and adopted the Report  at its meeting held on the 9 th  February, 2010. 
 
 
 
 
  SITARAM  YECHURY 
 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman,  
February 9, 2010 Department-related  Parliamentary Standing  
Magha 20, 1931 (Saka)   Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture. 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

REPORT  
  The Report of the Committee deals with the Action  Taken by the Government on the 
observations/recommendations as contained in its On e-Hundred and Forty-ninth  Report on Development of  Tourism 
Infrastructure and Amenities for the Commonwealth G ames 2010 which was presented to both the Houses of  
Parliament on 23 rd  October, 2008. 
2.  Action Taken Replies have been received from th e Ministries of Tourism on the 17 
th 
 August 2009, Civil Aviation 
on the 24 
th 
 August 2009, Urban Development on the 26 
th 
 August 2009, Government of NCT of Delhi on the 6 
th 
 January, 
2010 and from Ministry of Culture on 4 
th 
 February, 2010 in respect of all the observations/ recommendations contained 
in the Report, which have been categorized as follows: 
(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been a ccepted by the Department: 
 Para No.19,   Total- 1 
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committ ee does not desire to pursue in view of the Departm ent 
replies: 
 Para Nos. 18,27  Total-2 
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich replies of the Department have not been accepte d by 
the Committee: 
 Para Nos. 14,20,27,28,29,44,57,68,73,90 and 92 Tot al-11 
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of whi ch final replies of the Department are still awaited: 
 Para Nos.15,81 and 95 Total-3 
3.  The Committee desires that final replies in res pect of the recommendations, which have been catego rized as 
interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest. 
4.  On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Co mmittee has made observations on each item of Actio n 
taken/proposed to be taken by the concerned Ministr ies. The recommendations of the Committee contained  in the One 
Hundred and Forty-ninth Report, action taken thereo n by the Ministries and recommendations/observation s of the 
Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs. 
5.  The Committee notes that during the Commonwealt h Games a large number of tourists are expected int o India 
besides the participants. The Committee feels that the Commonwealth Games would provide us good opport unity to 
showcase our rich cultural heritage and achievement s of the contemporary India to the International co mmunity, that 
would act as catalyst for development of infrastruc ture and capacity building. The success of Commonwe alth Games 
will not only position India as a multifaceted destination but will bring economic returns through business and tourism. 
The Committee, therefore, calls upon the Government  and all the stakeholders to make concerted efforts  for creating 
best of the facilities and infrastructure, renovati on and better up-keep of our tourism and ancient si tes, improving road 
and air connectivity and safety and security of the  tourist and providing adequate accommodation at re asonable prices. 
The Committee also recommends that Delhi being the Centre of important literary and cultural activitie s, should 
refurbish its Libraries, Museums, Art Galleries, Ha ats, etc., for showcasing its rich and varied cultu ral and intellectual 
heritage. 
       (Recommendations at Para 4 of the 149th Report)  
 

Replies of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India and Government of NCT of Delhi  
6.  Development and promotion of tourist destinatio ns is primarily undertaken by the State Government/  Union 
Territory Administrations. The Ministry of Tourism,  however provides financial assistance for tourism projects on the 
basis of proposals received from them subject to av ailability of funds and interse priority. Ministry of Tourism has 
written to Government of NCT of Delhi and Ministry of Culture to take appropriate steps in this direct ion in order to 
facilitate the free movement of tourists to the mon uments and also provide delay free access. The Mini stry of Tourism 
along with the Ministry of Culture would be introdu cing the provision of extending bulk ticketing for monuments well 
in advance to the industry stakeholders viz.  hotels, tour operators and travel agents. In view of the shortage of qualified 
guides at the monuments, a tripartite agreement bet ween the Ministries of Tourism and Culture and the industry 
stakeholders has been proposed for the introduction  of audio guides at identified A.S.I. monuments. Fu rther, it is 
proposed to introduce hygienically maintained toile ts at A.S.I. monuments which would be set up by the  Ministry of 
Tourism and thereafter maintained by the industry s takeholders. Ministry of Tourism has noted the obse rvations of the 
Committee and letters have been sent to the Government of NCT of Delhi and others. 
Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation Government of NCT of Delhi  
7.  Delhi Tourism is in the process for setting up of Soft Adventure Park at Sanjay Lake in East Delhi , Tourism 
Complex with Camping facility at Kangan Heri and Soft Adventure Park at NH-8 near Shiv Murti. The facilities would 
be ready before Commonwealth Games 2010. 
8.  Delhi Tourism is also in the process for settin g up of web portal for its various facilities vide which airline ticket, 
package tours, accommodation etc. would be available online. 
9.  Delhi Tourism has widely publicized the Bed & B reakfast scheme in which accommodation at reasonabl e cost 
would be made available to the visitors to the capital. 
10.  The literature and pamphlet of tourist nature is being upgraded by Delhi Tourism and would also b e made 
available at the Commonwealth Games venues besides positioning of touch screen kiosk at important plac es of tourist 
interest giving information related to tourism in and around Delhi. 
11.  Delhi Tourism also plans to upgrade/refurbish its Dilli Haat INA before Commonwealth Games 20l0. 
12.  A number of cultural programmes at various pla ces in Delhi before and during Commonwealth Games have also 
planned with the help of various academies of Government of NCT of Delhi. 
Department of Archaeology Government of NCT of Delhi  
13.  Department of Archaeology is maintaining few m onuments of local importance which have very little  potential 
for the National/International tourists. The monume nts of National importance and World Heritage Sites  are under the 
jurisdiction of Archaeological Survey of India, Gov ernment of India. However, the Department has selec ted 14 
monuments which fall on the route of Commonwealth G ames 2010 and is making necessary arrangements for their 
conservation and illumination through INTACH under the MoU entered by Department of Archaeology.  
Delhi Police  
14.  Delhi Police has prepared a security plan for Delhi which includes upgraded security of the city besides venue 
specific arrangements for the Commonwealth Games 20 10. Delhi Police is mobilizing its manpower by new 
recruitment and training, mobilization from CPOs an d other States through MHA for manpower deployment during 
CG-20l0. The upgraded security of Delhi will also i nclude tourist places within Delhi. For better policing and ensuring 
visible presence on the ground, Delhi Police has created 2 new districts, 12 new Sub-Divisions, 42 new Police Stations, 

increased the number of PCR vans, increased traffic  patrol, and surveillance over criminals. As such g round level 
police presence would be enhanced and prompt response would be available to public in general. 
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
15.  The Committee has learnt that the common ticket/adv ance ticket for visiting monuments under ASI has 
been in the process. The Ministry should ensure tha t the system worked without any flaw and was advert ised 
through print & electronic media. The Committee also desires to know the current status of the actions  planned 
by various departments of the Government of NCT of Delhi as mentioned above.  
16.  The Committee notes that there are adequate fu nds available with the Ministry of Tourism under in frastructure 
upgradation of tourism destination schemes. However , the, Committee notes with concern that no proposa ls from the 
Delhi Government for development of infrastructure and capacity building including creation and renova tion of 
hospitality facilities, modernization of tourism si tes, etc., was submitted/pending with the Ministry of Tourism till 
November 2008. The Committee feels that since the Commonwealth Games are drawing closer, so many projects have 
yet to be initiated, let alone completed. In such a situation, absence of any proposal from the NCT of Delhi surprises the 
Committee. The Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry of Tourism to impress upon the Government of Delhi 
and also the Government of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana a nd Rajasthan for submitting projects proposals for developing 
tourism infrastructure including hotel accommodatio n for the Games and release the funds at the earlie st for 
implementing the development works on time.   
(Para 8 ibid ) 
Reply of Ministry of Tourism, Government of India  
17.  Ministry of Tourism has impressed upon the Gov ernment of Delhi and also comments of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana 
and Rajasthan for submitting project proposals for developing tourism infrastructure in the wake of the Commonwealth 
Games 2010. Some more project proposals have been s anctioned to these States by the Ministry as under (amount 
sanctioned in lakh): 
1. Development of Ajmer-Pushkar Rs. 1069.68 
 as a mega project in Rajasthan  
2. Development of soft Adventure Park at Rs. 451.82  
 Sanjay Lake, Delhi  
3. Conservation and Dev. of Amer Rs. 485.39 
 Palace, Jaipur  
4. Development of Nahargarh Fort, Jaipur Rs. 432.06  
5. Integrated Development of Panipat-Kurukshetra- R s. 1545.22 
 Pinjore Circuit, Haryana (Phase II)  
  
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
18.  The Committee notes that the NCT of Delhi, Uttar Pr adesh and Rajasthan have submitted proposals. The 
Committee recommends that the matter should be take n up at the higher level, so that the proposals are  
expedited. The Committee may also be apprised of th e progress made in materializing the above projects , the 
quantity of work completed so far, the percentage o f work remaining to be completed and the targeted d ate of 
completions of the entire projects.  

19.  The Committee notes that the Government of Raj asthan is utilizing the opportunity for promotion of tourism and 
introducing various packages for the guests/tourist s visiting Rajasthan during the games. The Committe e recommends 
the Ministry of Tourism to provide adequate funds t o the Government of Rajasthan for promotion of vari ous tourism 
products in the State. It also recommends that the tax incentives/benefits as provided to the hotels i n the National 
Capital Region (NCR) of Delhi may suitably be extended to the hotels in Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and 
Rajasthan, so as to remove the imbalance in the dem and and supply of hotel rooms’ inventory. The Commi ttee also 
recommends that the Government of Rajasthan should make concerted efforts and coordinate with the Mini stry of 
Tourism (for promotional support), Ministry of Civi l Aviation (for introduction of more international flights to and 
from Jaipur and development of Airports and air con nectivity from Ajmer and Kota) and Ministry of Rail ways (for 
increasing the speed of the trains and double linin g of rail line between Delhi and Jaipur). The State  Government 
should also impress upon the hotels in the State to  take adequate security measures such as installing  x-ray machines 
for screening of baggage which is a must in the present scenario. (Para 13 ibid ) 
Reply of Ministry of Tourism, Government of India  
20.  Ministry of Tourism besides sanctioning of meg a project in Rajasthan (Ajmer Pushkar) at the total  amount of 
Rs.1069.68 lakh has also provided central financial  assistance amounting to Rs.7.5 crore in 2008-09 fo r Royal Palace 
on Wheels Luxury Train to promote tourism in Rajast han. The recommendations of the Committee has been conveyed 
to the Government of Rajasthan and Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of Railways. Development and promotion of 
tourist destinations is primarily undertaken by the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. Details of funds 
sanctioned by Ministry of Tourism to the State of Rajasthan for the development of tourism during last three years is as 
under: 
Years Amount sanctioned (Rs. In lakh) 
 Rajasthan Uttar Pradesh Haryana Madhya Pradesh 
2006-07 903.94 3544.46 1836.16 3609.78 
2007-08 1554.46 1399.63 2250.43 3825.75 
2008-09 2495.49 3839.64 2495.49 3071.66 
  
21.  In the Income Tax Act 2007-08, Section 80-ID w as introduced to give encouragement to 2, 3 and 4 s tar Hotels 
and Convention Centres of a minimum seating capacity of 3,000 persons being set up in the National Capital Region of 
Delhi, Gurgaon, Faridabad by March 2010 though the Commonwealth Games are to be held in October 2010, a Tax 
Holiday of five years was granted to these hotels t hat would be operational before March 31, 2010. How ever, letters 
has been written to Department of Revenue, Ministry  of Finance, Ministry of Railways and Ministry of C ivil Aviation 
flagging this issue. 
22.  On the request of the Ministry of Tourism, the  Finance Minister having regard to the significant rise in tourist 
arrivals, especially for cultural tourism, had in t he budget of 2008-09 granted a five year holiday fr om income tax to 
two, three or four star hotels that are established  in specified districts which have UNESCO-declared ‘World Heritage 
Sites’. The hotel should be constructed and start f unctioning during the period April 1,2008 to March 31, 2013. This 
incentive is not applicable to the revenue districts of Mumbai and Delhi. 

23.  Ministry of Tourism has recently reviewed and revised its Guidelines for Classification of hotels  wherein the 
issues of safety and security have been addressed viz.  X Ray machines, under belly scanners for vehicles,  metal 
detectors, verification of staff and service providers, etc. based on the star category. 
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
24.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry  and hopes that the State Governments would take 
the advantage of various schemes to boost tourist arrivals in the State.   
25.  While going around the Amber Fort, the Committ ee saw preparation for some film shooting by erecti ng big sets. 
The Committee was assured that it was not going to cause any damage to the monuments. The Committee’s 
apprehension came true just few days after when it was reported that a part of wall inside the monumen ts came 
crashing down. The Committee recommends that while allowing any activity including commercial in the monuments, 
which should necessarily be remain very exceptional, the Governments must ensure that safety, security, originality and 
cleanliness of the monuments is not impaired upon and no damages of any kind is caused.  
(Para 14 ibid ) 
Reply of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India  
26.  The Archaeological Survey of India allows only  cultural events to be organized in the selected mo numents 
subject to the terms and conditions laid down by th e Director General. Utmost care is taken by the sta ff of the ASI 
posted at the monuments/sites for the safety, secur ity and cleanliness of the monuments/sites during a ny such event. 
ASI shall take extra care during any cultural event that will be organized during the Common- wealth Games 2010. 
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
27.  The Committee finds the reply to be rather cryptic that does not answer to specific event referred by it.  
28.  The Committee notes that the conservation work  is being carried out in Amber Fort by Amer Develop ment 
Authority. The Committee however, desires that the concerned agencies be cautioned not to destroy/alter the originality 
while making effort to renovate the monuments. The Committee also notes with concern that the conditio n of 
monuments like Jantar Mantar and Albert Hall is not  upto the mark and desires that Amer Development Au thority 
should provide funds for their maintenance and upkeep. (Para 15 ibid ) 
Reply of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India  
29.  The concerns of the Committee have been convey ed to the State Government of Rajasthan. 
Reply of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India  
30.  It is hereby clarified that mandate of the Sta te Level Implementation Committee (SLIC), which have been set up 
as advisory bodies part of the National Mission on Monuments & Antiquities operational process, does n ot include 
conservation or protection works of monuments. Sinc e the monuments mentioned namely, Jantar Mantar and  Albert 
Hall in Jaipur are under State protection, it was f elt that a body like SLIC would provide appropriate  forum to convey 
the concern of the Standing Committee so that the State Government can initiate necessary steps in this regard. 
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
31.  The Committee desires to know the reaction of the G overnment of Rajasthan in this regard and 
recommends that follow up action should be pursued with Government of Rajasthan.  
32.  The Committee notes that a large number of per sons were likely to stay in the vicinity of Delhi during the games 
and the city of Taj Mahal is gearing up to meet the  expected tourists rush during the CWG 2010. The Co mmittee also 
notes that the Government of Uttar Pradesh is asses sing and preparing the infrastructural needs of the  city to 

accommodate around a million tourists likely to vis it the Taj Mahal during the Games. The Committee fe els that there 
is a need for expansion of hotels as more rooms would be required to accommodate the tourist and recommends that the 
Government should come up with some concessional/incentive packages to motivate the hoteliers to add rooms to their 
existing structures. The Committee recommends that the guidelines for funding existing hotels structur es needs to be 
looked into and the Government should amend the gui delines to provide financial assistance to the hote ls which are 
under construction. The State Governments of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan should be provided Central grants 
in order to meet the shortfall in hotel accommodation.  
(Para 18 ibid ) 
Reply of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India  
33.  Construction of hotels is primarily a private sector activity. In order to overcome the shortage of accommodation 
in the country, Ministry of Tourism has been in reg ular touch with the State Governments and the vario us Land 
Owning Agencies for creation of land banks. These a gencies have also been asked to allocate land on Jo int Venture/ 
Revenue Sharing basis and also to provide incentives and benefits to facilitate the growth of the accommodation sector 
in the country. They have also been requested to in crease the FAR/FSI in respect of the existing hotel s. As a result, 
various incentives/measures have been announced by the Government to encourage the growth of hotel roo ms in the 
NCR. As a result, the Ministry of Urban Development  has announced grant of additional Floor Area Ratio  (FAR) to 
hotels in Delhi except Lutyens Bungalow Zone, from 150 to 225. 
34.  Hotels of two, three and four star category th at are established in Agra are eligible for the 5 y ear Income Tax 
Holiday declared in the budget of 2008-09 being located in UNESCO declared World Heritage sites. 
35.  The External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) upto U S $ 100 million has also been allowed by Ministry of Finance 
in solving the liquidity crunch being faced by the hotel industry for setting up new hotel projects. 
36.  Details of funds sanctioned by Ministry of Tou rism to the State of Rajasthan for the development of tourism 
during last three years is as under: 
                                                  
Years Amount sanctioned (Rs. in lakh) 
 Rajasthan Uttar Pradesh Haryana 
2006-07 903.94 3544.46 1836.16 
2007-08 1554.46 1399.63 2250.43 
2008-09 2495.49 3839.64 2495.49 
  
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
37.  The Committee notes the steps taken in making arran gements for more rooms. However, the Committee 
feels that it needs to be taken up in a time bound manner. The Committee desires to know the funds uti lized, 
scheme-wise, by the State Governments during the above period.  
38.  The Committee notes the problems like long and  arduous train/road journey from New Delhi to Agra,  lack of 
tourist buses attached to the railway stations in A gra and Delhi, inadequate access from Agra Cantt. R ailway station to 
Taj Mahal and Sikandara, poor condition of the batt ery operated vehicles, lack of adequate parking, ca feteria, security 
check, long queues for tickets, drinking water, toi lets, luggage room, facilitation centres, etc. The Committee feels that 
these are not big issues and can be resolved by way  of better coordination among different agencies es pecially the 

Ministry of Defence for construction of underpass i n Shahganj area for proper road connectivity to Taj  Mahal. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends the Government to find immediate solutions to these problems and intr oduce easy 
ticketing procedures like prior ticketing, e-ticket ing, composite tickets, flexible tickets, group tic kets, tatkal system, 
transit passes system, etc. for gaining entry to Ta j Mahal, besides restructuring and strengthening of  the security. The 
drinking water, toilet facilities and facilitation centres should be provided outside the Taj Mahal to  facilitate the 
tourists. The problems of guides should be resolved  by the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Government  of Uttar 
Pradesh with mutual interaction.   
  (Para 19 ibid ) 
Reply of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India  
39.  The concerns of the Committee regarding the pr oblems in accessibility of Agra City have been communicated to 
the Ministry of Railways and Transport. Regarding t he poor tourist infrastructure in the city, the Sta te Government, 
ASI and the concerned authorities at the district l evel are being impressed upon to bring about tangible changes so that 
to make the destination world class. Secretary (Tourism) himself is monitoring these concerns and a se ries of meetings 
with the State Government, District Authorities, Fo rest Departments, ASI, Ministry of Culture etc. hav e been taken by 
him and certain decisions reached to facilitate the tourists. 
40.  The Ministry of Tourism has requested State Go vernment and the Department of Road Transport and H ighways 
to improve the condition of State Road. An Inter- M inisterial Group on this issue of road connectivity  has been set up. 
Provision is being made for sales of entry tickets in advance for ASI sites to Government of India app roved Travel 
Trade members. Newly designated tickets are likely to be launched. It has also been discussed to have clean washroom 
facility for international travellers at world heri tage monuments to be run and managed by IATO and ot her trade 
associations. On the issue of problem of guides and  other difficulties faced by Travel Trade members, stress was given 
on the introduction of hand held audio guide in at least 6 foreign languages besides English to cope up with the issue of 
shortage of guides. 
Reply of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India  
41.  It is true that the number of buses attached t o the Agra Cantt. railway station are not adequate in proper line to the 
tourist inflow, hence there is a possibility to imp rove the public transport system at the important r ailway station at 
Agra. ASI has recently introduced common entry tick ets at all the ticketed monuments under their juris diction 
including Taj Mahal in order to reduce the queue at  the ticketed window at the monument. The drinking water, toilet 
and clock room facilities are being provided to the tourists visiting at Taj Mahal. 
42.  The archaeological Survey of India has propose d for visitor’s centre on the eastern and western g ates of Taj 
Mahal for which the design concept has been formula ted by Taj Mahal conservation collaborative. The pr oposal is 
under consideration before the Hon’ble Supreme Cour t of India wherein the hon’ble apex court has direc ted ASI to 
demonstrate the power-point presentation on their p roposal before the Hon’ble Justice Shri Kapadia and  Shri Altaf 
Ahmed on 11.1.2010. The Hon’ble Justice have apprec iated the proposal mooted by ASI for providing faci litation 
centre which should facilitate the visitors for smooth entry, security checks, cloak room, drinking water, toilet facilities, 
audio guide, photographers, kiosks, etc. within the facilitation centre on the western and eastern gate of Taj Mahal. The 
proposal has been approved in principle by the Hon’ble Justices. 
43.  Tourists visiting Fatehpur Sikri, after seeing  Taj Mahal have to cross almost the whole Agra city  and the narrow 
roads sometimes became overcrowded. In order to ove rcome this situation, an underpass is planned in th e Shahganj 
area for an easy communication of tourists. The Sha hganj area is within the control of the cantonment board, therefore 
the agencies involved for providing an underpass ar e the Ministry of Defence, Directorate of Defence e states, Ministry 
of Railways, and State Government of U.P. and Minis try of Tourism, Government of U.P. In this regard t he 

recommendations and the observations made by the Pa rliamentary Standing Committee are being sent to co ncerned 
agencies for taking further necessary action so that not only the issue is resolved but also a sigh of  relief is provided to 
the tourists who are on their way to Fatehpur Sikri. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
44.  The Committee feels that ferry services like those operated by Delhi Metro Rail Corporation may be 
introduced between Agra Cantt. railway station and Taj Mahal so that the tourists were not put to any trouble 
by unscrupulous elements at the railway station and  in the premises of Taj Mahal. Further coordination  with 
various agencies should be closely monitored and a nodal agency made to implement the steps.  
45.  The Committee notes the Ministry’s efforts to issue  common entry ticket. The Committee desires that th e 
process of setting up of facilitation centre should be expedited and the construction of underpass should be taken 
up with the concerned agencies with a view to present Agra in a better way to the visiting tourists.  
46.  The Committee notes that the view of Taj from the other side of Yamuna from Mehtab Bagh may be a thrilling 
experience for the tourists during full moon night that creates a view of Taj being black. The Committ ee recommends 
that viewing of Taj Mahal from this side should be promoted and permission for adequate parking and to ilet facilities 
should be provided there. The Committee desires tha t in maintaining the monuments, environmental devel opments 
including horticulture works and landscaping, civic  amenities for tourists and display of cultural not ice boards and 
signages should be taken care of. The Government should make concerted efforts to involve public and corporate sector 
for the purpose. The Committee also recommends that  a survey should be conducted by the Government to ascertain

DEMOLTION  OF  LAL  MAHAL  
162.  The Committee pointed out the dismal picture of state of affairs relating to the poor management  and upkeep of 
the monuments which is evident through the demoliti on of Lal Mahal. The Committee is perturbed to note  that the 
concerned agencies are shying away from their respo nsibility and passing the buck and blame each other . The ASI has 
washed its hands off claiming that Lal Mahal was no t a protected monument and that the MCD should have  preserved 
it. The MCD claims that it was not on the heritage list and it was protected in the INTACH list as it cares about 
unprotected ones. The Ministry of Urban Development does not know anything about the incident, although it has been 
much highlighted in the media. The ASI is being blamed for inaction despite Lal Mahal being in the Zafar Hasan’s List 
for the Central Protection. The State Government is  being blamed for not notifying monuments like the Lal Mahal 
despite a list sent to them three years ago and the  police have not been able to nab the culprits so f ar. This shows the 
utter lack of coordination and confusion between di fferent agencies of the Union as well as the State Government and 
the local bodies. In this connection a communicatio n was sent to the Ministries of Tourism and Culture  to provide 
information about the role of different agencies in  protection of the monuments in Delhi and NCR regio n, but the 
Committee is constrained to say that no response was given by the Ministries till the adoption of the report. 
(Para 90 ibid ) 
Reply of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India  
163.  Lal Mahal is neither protected by the Central  Government nor the Government of National Capital Territory of 
Delhi. Lal Mahal and its premises were under use fo r residential purposes. Even after demolition of ol d structures 
located within the premises, to make way for some m odem construction, traces are still visible. Immedi ately after the 

construction activities started at Lal Mahal, the Archaeological Survey of India had lodged a complaint with the Police 
Station against construction in the prohibited area  of Chausath Khambha, a centrally protected monumen t, located in 
Basti Nizamuddin, in violation of the Ancient Monum ents & Archaeological Sites & Remains Rules, 1959 a nd 
Notification 1992. As per the rule, no construction  is permissible in 100 m area of any centrally prot ected monument. 
The police complaint was followed by letters to Dy.  Commissioner, Delhi Police and Dy. Commissioner, M unicipal 
Corporation Delhi with the request to stop unauthor ized construction activities at the site. Subsequen tly, show-cause 
notice was also issued to the offender under rule 3 8 of the Ancient Monuments & Archaeological Sites &  Remains 
Rules, 1959. The ASI declares ancient monuments, ar chaeological sites and remains as protected under t he Ancient 
Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act,  1958 only when the same is found worthy of nationa l 
importance. In Delhi, to be specific, there are a l arge number of monuments out of which only 174 have  been declared 
as of national importance. The monuments other than those declared protected by the Central Government had not been 
considered for declaration as protected earlier dul y considering their historical, archaeological or a rtistic importance. 
Since archaeology falls in the concurrent list, it becomes the responsibility of the State Government to declare the 
monuments other than those protected by the Central Government as State protected, more so, when the Government of 
National Capital Territory of Delhi has its own Act  in force. The Central Government declares an ancie nt monument, 
archaeological site or remains as of national impor tance under Section 4 of the Ancient Monuments & Ar chaeological 
Sites & Remains Act, 1958 only when the same, in it s opinion, is found to be of national importance, a fter issuing a 
notification declaring its intention in the Officia l Gazette and inviting objections front interested persons giving two 
months notice. Subsequent to issue of notification,  the interested persons are at liberty to file obje ctions against the 
intention of the Central Government. The Central Go vernment after the expiry of two months period and considering 
the objections so received declare the said monumen t as of national importance by issuing a notificati on again in the 
Official Gazette. The procedure to declare a monume nt as of national importance is a time consuming pr ocess. More 
so, when its ownership is private. In cases where t he ownership is private, the Central Government is required to enter 
into an agreement with the owner for the maintenanc e of the monument as per Section 6 of the Ancient M onuments & 
Archaeological Sites & Remains Act, 1958. 
164.  In Delhi the ancient monuments and heritage buildings fall under following categories--- 
  Centrally protected monuments, 
  State protected monuments, and 
  Unprotected monuments. 
165.  While the responsibility of protection of cen trally protected monuments rests with the Central G overnment 
through the Archaeological Survey of India, the Govt. of NCT Delhi is responsible for State protected monuments. The 
unprotected monuments and heritage buildings fall u nder the purview of Municipal Corporation of Delhi/ New Delhi 
Municipal Council/Cantonment Board, since they are required to list such buildings as heritage propert ies and the 
responsibility for these protection lies with the respective civic agency as per the area under jurisdiction.

to make our cities beautiful. Agra need special att ention not only in terms of beautification, but als o for providing 
smooth connectivity of world famous monuments there. Let there be dedicated heritage corridors which s hould be free 

from all types of encroachments and connect the monuments of the national importants either to National Highways or 
the State Highways. To begin with the monuments of Agra i.e. Fatehpur Sikri, Taj Mahal, I’timad-ud-Daula Tomb and

of the States to make Commonwealth Games a successful event.

INTRODUCTION  
  I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary  Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism 
and Culture, having been authorised by the Committe e to present on its behalf, do hereby present this  
One Hundred and Fifty Fourth Report on “Demands for Grants 2010-11 of the Ministry of Tourism”. 
2.  The Committee, at its meeting held on the 26th March, 2010, considered the subject and heard 
the Secretary and other officials of the Ministry of Tourism. 
3.  The Committee wishes to express its thanks to t he officers of the Ministry of Tourism for 
placing before the Committee the material and infor mation desired in connection with the subject and 
for clarifying the points raised by the Members. 
4.. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 7th April, 2010. 
 
 
  SITARAM  YECHURY 
 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman,  
April  7, 2010 Department-related  Parliamentary Standing  
Chaitra 17, 1932 ( Saka )  Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

REPORT  
  Tourism plays a pivotal role in the over all deve lopment of a country. It is an important vehicle 
for wide-ranging socio-economic and cultural contac ts amongst the peoples. Tourism is, in fact, a 
multi sectoral activity characterized by multiple s ervices provided by a range of agencies. It is the 
largest service industry in the country. Its importance lies in its having a cascading effect on economic 
development. A wide array of areas such as hospital ity and entertainment, sports, religion, culture, 
adventure, education, health, etc. get impetus. Mob ility of the people promotes cultural cohesion and 
social bonding that creates a durable social fabric . While the Government of India plays a crucial rol e 
in making provision for tourism infrastructure and skill development, private sector also has a major 
role in this sector. 
2.  India’s performance in tourism sector shows a g rowth from 2.38 million in 2002 to 5.28, million 
in 2008 as regards foreign tourist arrival. However , the numbers declined to 5.11 million in 2009 
which is about 3.3 per cent less than that of the previous year. This reduction was mainly due to global 
slowdown, terrorist activities, H1N1 influenza pand emic, etc. Foreign Exchange Earnings from 
tourism has increased from Rs.15,064 crore in 2002 to Rs.54,960 crore in 2009. The growth rate in 
earnings in 2009 vis-a-vis  2008 was 8.3 per cent. The important activity with  the Ministry of Tourism 
in 2010, is its preparedness for the XIX Commonwealth Games. 
3.  The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency for  the formulation of national policies and 
programmes and for the coordination of actudies of various Central Government agencies, State 
Governments/Union territories and the Private Secto r for the development and promotion of tourism 
in the country. The Ministry of Tourism plays a cru cial role in coordinating and supplementing the 
efforts of the State/Union territories Governments,  catalyzing private investment, strengthening 
promotional and marketing efforts and in providing trained manpower resources. 
4.   The tourism industry, which is of particular s ignificance to India, has contributed to national 
integration, preservation of natural as well as cul tural environments and enrichment of the social and  
cultural lives of people. Tourism also encourages p reservation of monuments and heritage properties 
and helps the survival of arts forms, crafts and cu lture. However, it is not getting its due share in the 
Indian economy in spite of contributing to GDP. The Committee observes that the tourism 
resources of India have the potential to generate s ignificantly higher levels of demand from the 
domestic and international markets, and if exploited in a sustainable manner, it can prove to be 
an engine of growth for the economy. The Committee,  therefore, recommends that the 
Government should provide more funds for promoting tourism and tapping the vast and varied 
potential - modern and ancient.

10.  The Committee notes that during the year 2009-10, t he allocation was reduced to 
Rs.950.00 crore at RE stage, out of which, an amoun t of Rs.776.16 crore is likely to be utilized 
till Feb., 2010. Thus, 19%. of allocation is likely to be utilized in just one month. The Committee 
does not approve the practice of last minute spendi ng at the fag end of the financial year. The 
Committee in its earlier Reports, has conveyed this  feeling to the Ministries concerned. The 
Ministry should follow the existing norms strictly to ensure that the funds are utilized, as far as 
possible, evenly throughout the year. The Committee also does not find any reason for reducing 
the allocation at RE stage. Tourism is the largest service industry with a contribution of 6.23% 
of the GDP and 8.78% of the total employment in Ind ia. Since Tourism projects are 
implemented by the States, there is need to sensitize them to ensure optimum utilization of funds

TOURIST INFRASTRUCTURE  
11.  This provision relates to the expenditure on c reation of Infrastructure facilities on constructio n 
of budget accommodation, wayside amenities, Tourist  Reception, Centres, refurbishment of 
monuments, Special Tourism Projects, Adventure and Sports facilities, Sound and Light Shows, 
Illuminations of moments, providing for improvement  in solid waste management and sewerage 
management, improvement of surroundings, signages, procurement of equipment directly also relates 
to the Large Revenue Generating Projects generating revenue through levy of fees or user charges like 

Tourist Trains, Cruise vessels, Cruise terminals, C onvention Centres, Golf Courses etc. and creation 
of land bank for hotels to provide the hotel accomm odation in the country by purchasing land and 
build hotels through Public Private Partnerships. T he provision also includes Externally Aided 
Projects (including UNDP Endogenous Tourism Projects), Assistance to Central agencies for Tourism 
Infrastructure Development and for Construction of Building of Indian Institute of Skiing and 
Mountaineering at Gulmerg.

Development for Destination and Circuits during 2007-08, 2008-09, 2009-10 and the allocation during

13.  Assistance for large revenue generating projec ts include tourism projects in PPP mode and 
partnership with Government and semi-Government agencies. The Ministry proposed to undertake 4-5 
projects during 2010-11 and Rs.16 crore is the outlay for this. The period of completion of the projects 
is 2-3 years from the date of commencement. Rs.5 crore and 15 crore were sanctioned during 2009-10 
and 2010-11 respectively. 
14.  Under the Product/infrastructure development f or Destination and Circuits a world-class tourist 
infrastructure facility at the identified circuits,  destinations and rural sites are proposed. One cir cuit 
and two destinations per State are proposed to be t aken up in consultation with the concerned State 
Governments. The projects are proposed to be comple ted within 3 years time since the date of 
commencement. The review of Annual Plan 2009-10 sta tes that 160 infrastructure projects including 
rural tourism have been sanctioned up to September,  2009. Also 164 new projects were sanctioned 
during 2008-09 with a sanction of Rs.522 crore whic h included Rs.89 crore sanctioned for the N-E 
States. 
15.  The Committee notes that a country as vast and  diverse as India can best be covered in clusters - 
tourist spots grouped together so that they are wel l-connected for all travellers, especially 
international. However, the only popular circuit is  Delhi-Agra Jaipur. Most of the new circuits are in  
proposal stage. There is lack of infrastructure support and connectivity in these circuits. 
16.  The Committee, however, finds that in the case of u tilization of fund for 
product/infrastructure development for circuit duri ng 2007-08, 2008-09 and 2009-10, 
expenditure has been more than what was allocated i n the budget. The Committee recommends 
that if the schemes are chalked out well in time by the Ministry, they can approach the Planning 
Commission /Ministry of Finance for allocation of more funds at BE stage itself.  
17.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry shou ld make all out efforts for the 
development of a particular circuit which is approv ed for implementation. Moreover various 

States should coordinate and develop inter-State ci rcuits. Southern and Central circuits need to 
be developed with more emphasis on travel connectivity.  
18.  Creation of land bank for hotels is another it em included this year also and for that Rs.1 crore is 
the outlay during 2010-11 to tackle the issue of shortage of hotel accommodation all over the country. 
The aim was to purchase land from the land owning a gencies and construct the hotels under PPP 
mode. Equal amount were sanctioned during previous two years also for the same purpose but the 
statements given by the Ministry of Tourism says that the project is yet to be taken off. 
19.  On asked about the reasons for non utilization  of funds for the creation of land banks for hotels  
for the last two years, the Secretary, Ministry of Tourism has informed the Committee that they have 
been in regular touch with the State Governments an d various Land Owning Agencies for creation of 
land banks. The State Governments/UTs have been req uested not to resort to the auctioning of hotel 
sites as auctioning hotel sites at a very high rese rve price makes the project unviable, but give land on 
long lease, joint venture/revenue sharing basis or allot land like what is that done for industrial si tes, 
increase the F AR/FSI in respect of the existing hotels etc. 
20.  The Committee finds no justification for making pro vision of plan outlay in the Budget 
under the Head-Creation of Land Bank for Hotels when the plan allocation remained unutilized 
since the inception of the scheme. The Committee, t herefore, recommended the scheme may be 
reviewed and modified with view to ensure that deve lopment of accommodation for tourists is 
not affected.  
21.  Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Inf rastructure development to ensure works like 
illumination/preservation of monuments, development of cruise terminals etc., the assistance is given 
to the Archaeological Survey of India, Port Trust o f India, ITDC etc. During 2010-11an amount of 
Rs.24.00 crore was allocated. Rs.10 crore and Rs.12  crore were expended for the same during the 
years 2009-10 and 2008-09. 
22.  The Committee came to know that ITDC is doing the i llumination work in some of the 
major monuments in Delhi. Further, ITDC also host l ight and sound show in some of the 
monuments which is being appreciated. Particularly Delhi will be hosting XIX Commonwealth 
Games this year the light and Sound show can be use d to attract more tourist and to acquaint 
them with the history as well as majesty of our fam ous monuments. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should ensure that thi s year sufficient funds are allocated to 
ITDC for this job.  
23.  To supplement the efforts of the State Governm ents in augmentation of infrastructure facilities 
for the tourists, Ministry of Tourism extends Centr al Financial Assistance for tourism projects for 
Infrastructure Destination Development to the pilgr im centres based on the proposals received form 
the State Governments as per the Scheme Guidelines.  The Ministry has sanctioned one mega project 
Development of Haridwar-Rishikesh- Munikireti-Swarg ashram, Uttarakhand in the year 2008-09 for 
48.62 crore.

25.  The Committee notes the projects and funds sanction ed to various States. However, the

26.  The Committee also came to know that Ministry of Tourism has set up goal that wayside 
facilities should be at 50km (intervals) on nationa l highways on either side of the road, 40km 
(intervals) on state highways and along hills every  30km and the States have been told to construct 
and oversee the upkeep of wayside amenities along h ighways/roads leading to tourist destinations. 
Wayside facilities will have three models: (i) toil ets/bathing places (ii) eateries and basic amenitie s 
alongside and (iii) restaurants with basic amenitie s. The wayside facilities can be developed with 
central financial assistance. 
27.  The way-side facilities may appear to be insignific ant things in comparison to other 
tourism infrastructure, these are, however, very important from the tourist’s point of view. The 
Committee desires that this scheme needs to be wide ly publicized and the States be impressed 
upon to take benefit from this. In fact, the Minist ry of Tourism should set target for each State 
and implementation of the scheme should be monitored in a time-bound manner.  
28.  The Ministry of Tourism informed that they hav e also prioritized projects in Uttarakhand for the 
year 2010-11 namely. Nirmal Gangotri Mega Project ( Circuit) (Rishikesh-Narendranagar-Chamba-
Uttarkashi- Bhatwari-Harsil-Gangotri) Development o f Panch Prayag-Srinagar (Kalimath) Tourism 
Circuit. In order to give a boost to the hospitalit y sector, the Government on the request of the 
Ministry of Tourism, had earlier announced a Five Y ear Tax Holiday under Section 80-ID of the 
Income Tax Act to new hotels of two, three and four star category and Convention Centres coming up 
between 1.4.07 to 31.03.2010 in the National Capita l Territory Region of Delhi and the districts of 
Faridabad, Gurgaon, Gautam Budh Nagar (NOIDA) and Ghaziabad. The last date for availing the Five 
Year Tax Holiday during the announcements of the Un ion Budget for the year 2010-2011 has been 
extended from 31.03.2010 to 31.07.2010. With a view  to boost the tourism industry, an investment 
linked deduction Under Section 35 AD to the hotel s ector allowing 100% deduction in respect of the 
whole of any expenditure of capital nature excludin g (land, goodwill and financial instruments) 
incurred during the year for establishing new hotel s of 2 star category and above, all over India has 
also been made in the Union Budget 2010-2011 announ cements. Under Section 35AD, the Assessee 
Company will be getting the entire expenditure qualifying under this as a deduction and will be saving 
the effective tax of 33.22%. 
29.  On being asked about the region-wise and State-wise  plans for tourism infrastructure 
development in the country, the Ministry of Tourism  replied that there was no such plan with 
them. The Committee, however, recommends that Ministry may consider evolving the approach 
for development of region/Statewise tourism infrastructure development in order to promote the 
domestic tourism more vigorously which has a great potential. The Committee is of the view 
that such approach may generate interest among the local people and Government of the State 
concerned which can ensure that speedy development and timely completion.  
30.  It appears that presently the infrastructure development is mainly focused on five star and 
such high cost accommodation which are out of commo n man’s access. So, the tax-holiday 
benefits and such concessions are ultimately not re aching to the majority. The Committee is of 

the view that Ministry of tourism should concentrat e on promoting accommodation for the 
domestic tourists who usually prefer affordable and  safe accommodation rather than the costly 
star hotels. The Committee, therefore, recommends t hat budget hotels aimed at the domestic 
tourists should also be given priority by the Minis try of Tourism and accordingly all the 
promotional measures and tax benefits should also t o be extended to the budget hotels and 
restaurants also.

resource development. The Government has not made s ufficient plan outlay under the head 
‘assistance for manpower training’. In the year 200 9-10, an amount of Rs. 100.70 crore was 
allocated. For the 2010-11 there is negligible increase in the plan outlay i.e. Rs. 102.50 crore. The

the Committee has not been informed whether any target has been fixed for completion of these 
institutes. The Committee feels that the huge shortage of about 1.9 lakhs can not be met only by

UGC and the technical institutions under AICTE may be encouraged to open courses on 
hospitality industry and necessary financial assist ance for infrastructural and other required

extended by the Ministry of Tourism to these agenci es as they have the men and material for

85.  The Ministry has informed that in order to ens ure safety and security of tourists, Ministry of 
Tourism has advised all the State Governments/Union  Territory Administrations to deploy Tourist 
Police in the States/Union Territories. Ministry of  Tourism in consultation with Ministry of Home 
Affairs, Ministry of Defence and Directorate Genera l of Resettlements has framed guidelines for 
formation of Tourist Security Organization (s) comp rising Ex-Servicemen, for the safety and security 
of the tourists. The guidelines have been sent alon g with the letter dated 02 
nd  May, 2008 of Hon’ble 
Minister to the State Governments / Union Territory Administrations. 
86.  Further, a detailed note along with the guidel ines for setting up of Tourist Facilitation and 
Security Organization comprising primarily of Ex-Se rvicemen in States/Union Territories for 
providing the safety and security to the tourists, under CFA Scheme was forwarded to the Planning 
Commission for in-principle approval. The matter ha s been taken up with the Deputy Chairman, 
Planning Commission vide  letter of Hon’ble Minister (Tourism and Housing an d Urban Poverty 
Alleviation) dated 02nd January, 2010. 
87.  The guidelines stipulate that the tourist poli ce be constituted from a pool of ex-servicemen 
maintained by the Director General of Resettlement. It will be a three-tier structure-state level, district 
level and destination level-which will be supervised by a Joint Committee comprising the State Home 
Secretary and the Tourism Secretary. The Chief Tour ist Warden will be a retired commissioned 
officer while the District Tourist Warden may be a retired Junior Commissioned Officer. The 
destination tourist warden will be preferably a sub eadar or equivalent the guideline state while 
maintaining that a working knowledge in spoken Engl ish is a prerequisite. The Governments of 
Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Goa, Kerala, Maharashtra , Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa, Uttar 
Pradesh, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Jammu an d Kashmir are reported to have deployed 
Tourists Police, in one form or the other. 

88.  The Committee is of the view that policing of touri sts is an important aspect and it should 
be given paramount importance to ensure that India is recognized as popular tourist 
destination. Many of the States have not constitute d the tourism police and wherever they are 
constituted it is just tokenism. The Committee, the refore recommends that all the State 
Governments may be pursued to create effective police mechanism to protect the tourists.

menace need to be prevented effectively. The Commit tee was informed that Ministry of Tourism 
received a draft of the “Delhi Prevention of Malpra ctice and Touting Bills 2009" from Ministry of

Tourism have also initiated several media. campaign s aimed at enhancing social awareness and to 
publicise "Atithi Devo Bhava" concept. 
91.  The Committee notes the initiative of the Governmen t in bringing “Delhi Prevention of 
Malpractice and Touting Bills 2009”. The Committee recommends that other State 
Governments may also be persuaded to bring out the similar legislations so that the menace of 
touts and middlemen are controlled throughout India.

ENVIRONMENTAL FRIENDLY INITIATIVES  
96.  As per a study on the impact of tourism promot ion measure on the habitat of wildlife in Corbett 
National Park it was found out that there is a grow ing trend towards travel to eco-tourism destinations 
like National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries. The Ministry of Tourism conducted a survey through the 
students of the Institute of Hotel Management, Pusa , New Delhi to consider the ground factors like 
anti environmental activities that hampers the peac eful living of the wild life. The survey was 
conducted from December 16, 2009 to December 22, 20 09 and the outcome had very revealing 
information about the misuse of opportunities in th e guise of tourism by the hoteliers and resort 
operators. 

97.  Based on the findings of Survey Report the Min istry of Tourism proposes to organize similar 
surveys at Kaziranga National Park. The Ministry of Tourism has informed that they held a meeting to 
plan a National Workshop for Sustainable Tourism Criteria for India to discuss the modalities with the 
various stakeholders of the Tourism industry.  
98.  The Committee recommends that the tourism should be  eco-friendly and it should not 
interfere with the ecosystem. The Committee also recommends that strict action should be taken 
against all who are violating the prescribed norms and setting hotels etc. in the restricted area, 
and ecologically sensitive forest areas.  
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN J&K  
99.  The Ministry informed that a number of proposa ls for development of tourism infrastructure 
have been received from the State Government of J&K  during the financial year 2009-10. After 
consideration of these projects as per the scheme g uidelines, inter se  priority and availability of funds 
19 projects were sanctioned to the Government of J& K in 2009-10. During the 11th Plan Ministry of 
Tourism has sanctioned 57 tourism projects, including fairs festival, for an amount of Rs.140.94 crore 
to the State of J&K. 
100.  The Committee notes that there is enough scope for linking the historical and religious 
place of Jammu and Kashmir in the world tourism by giving sufficient infrastructural facilities 
adequate publicity and authoritative information. T he Committee recommends that Bangus 
valley and Neelnag, (District Budgam) in Jammu and Kashmir-need to be developed as a major 
tourist destination.

101.  On asked about the LTC relaxation to travel b y air will be extended to people visiting Southern 
States as like done in the case of N-E Region and J ammu and Kashmir the Ministry of Tourism has 
informed that relaxation of Home Town LTC provision  has to be issued by the Ministry of Personnel 
and Training to encourage domestic tourists in the Southern States including Kerala. States in the 
Southern Region have been requested to furnish their comments in the matter. A request has also been 
sent to the Ministry of Civil Aviation to furnish their comments in the matter. 
102.  The Committee observes that LTC concessions for the Government employees has a major 
role in domestic tourism promotion. The scheme for a particular region should be kept live for a 
considerable period of time so that other concerned  agencies like Indian Airlines, hoteliers, 
Railways etc. could also introduce some long term m easures. It is also pertinent to mention that 
the LTC package as provided by the AI does not have  enough seat availability under the 
package and that employees some times not able to f ind a suitable itinerary. The matter need to 
be taken up with the Ministry of Civil Aviation.  
GENERAL OBSERVATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS  
103.  The Committee had observed that the present form in  which budget related data is given 
to the Committee while examining Demands for Grants of the Ministry does not provide a clear 
picture about actual performance/achievements during a particular year.  
104.  Domestic tourism is getting comparatively lesser importance by the Ministry, which leaves 
the most local tourism potential unexploited. More infrastructure development is needed, 
keeping in view the domestic tourists potential. The target set for each and every projects need a 

review and a more scientific approach should be ado pted. Even small countries are able to 
achieve their targets within a stipulated time, it is a matter of concern that India is lagging 
behind its project implementation ultimately resulting cost escalations and revenue losses.  
105.  The Committee also pointed out that travel by train  is an integral part of the domestic 
tourism. Moreover, many exclusive tourist trains have started plying exclusively for the tourists. 
The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism s hould coordinate with the Railway 
authorities in order to provide safe, secure and enjoyable to the tourists.  
106.  The Committee notes that connectivity to tourist de stination is the pivotal aspect of the 
development of tourism. Many of the areas which have huge tourism potential are left out by the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 
For instance, Thekkady and Bekal Fort are the two m ajor tourist destinations in Kerala. If 
helicopter services are started in these areas lot of tourists will be attracted to these areas and it  
will be a big boost for tourism in these two places . The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry of Tourism may take up with the Ministry o f Civil Aviation and Airport Authority of 
India to construct airstrips in Thekkady and Bekal Fort in Kerala.  
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS –– AT A GLANCE  
  The Committee observes that the tourism resources  of India have the potential to generate 
significantly higher levels of demand from the dome stic and international markets, and if 
exploited in a sustainable manner, it can prove to be an engine of growth for the economy. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Governmen t should provide more funds for 
promoting tourism and tapping the vast and varied potential - modern and ancient. (Para 4)  
BUDGETARV ALLOCATIONS AND ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2010-11 
  The Committee notes that during the year 2009-10,  the allocation was reduced to 
Rs.950.00 crore at RE stage, out of which, an amoun t of Rs.776.16 crore is likely to be utilized 
till Feb. 2010. Thus, 19% of allocation is likely t o be utilized in just one month. The Committee 
does not approve the practice of last minute spendi ng at the fag end of the financial year. The 
Committee in its earlier Reports, has conveyed this  feeling to the Ministries concerned. The 
Ministry should follow the existing norms strictly to ensure that the funds are utilized, as far as 
possible, evenly throughout the year. The Committee also does not find any reason for reducing 
the allocation at RE stage. Tourism is the largest service industry with a contribution of 6.23 % 
of the GDP and 8.78% of the total employment in Ind ia. Since Tourism projects are 
implemented by the States, there is need to sensitize them to ensure optimum utilization of funds 
and issuing user utilization certificates on time. The Ministry should make concerted efforts and 
evolve a coordination mechanism with the States.    
TOURIST INFRASTRUCTURE 
  The Committee, however, finds that in the case of  utilization of fund for 
product/infrastructure development for circuit duri ng 2007-08, 2008-09 and 2009-10, 
expenditure has been more than what was allocated i n the budget. The Committee recommends 
that if the schemes are chalked out well in time by the Ministry, they can approach the Planning 
Commission /Ministry of Finance for allocation of more funds at BE stage itself.             (Para 16)  
  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry sh ould make all out efforts for the 
development of a particular circuit which is approv ed for implementation. Moreover various 
States should coordinate and develop inter-state ci rcuits. Southern and central circuits need to 
be developed with more emphasis on travel connectivity.                                                     (Para 17)  
  The Committee finds no justification for making p rovision of plan outlay in the Budget 
under the Head-Creation of Land Bank for Hotels when the plan allocation remained unutilized 
since the inception of the scheme. The Committee, t herefore, recommended the scheme may be 
reviewed and modified with view to ensure that deve lopment of accommodation for tourists is 
not affected. 
(Para 20)  
  The Committee came to know that ITDC is doing the  illumination work in some of the 
major monuments in Delhi. Further, ITDC also host l ight and sound show in some of the 
monuments which is being appreciated. Particularly Delhi will be hosting XIX Commonwealth 
Games this year the light and Sound show can be use d to attract more tourist and to acquaint 
them with the history as well as majesty of our fam ous monuments. The Committee, therefore, 

recommends that the Ministry should ensure that thi s year sufficient funds are allocated to 
ITDC for this job. (Para 22)  
  The Committee notes the projects and funds sancti oned to various States. However, the 
Committee is not aware of the targets fixed for com pletion of these projects. It has also come to 
the notice of the Committee that in some cases proj ects received from the State Governments 
are not processed/ sanctioned in time which result in delay and non-utilisation of funds. The 
Committee, therefore recommends that the progress o f these projects need to be monitored 
regularly to ensure that there is no delay and cost overrun in the projects. (Para 25)  
  The way-side facilities may appear to be insignif icant things in comparison to other 
tourism infrastructure, these are, however, very important from the tourist’s point of view. The 
Committee desires that this scheme needs to be wide ly publicized and the States be impressed 
upon to take benefit from this. In fact, the Minist ry of Tourism should set target for each State 
and implementation of the scheme should be monitored in a time-bound manner. (Para 27)  
  The Committee, however, recommends that Ministry may consider evolving the approach 
for development of region/State-wise tourism infras tructure development in order to promote 
the domestic tourism more vigorously which has a great potential. The Committee is of the view 
that such approach may generate interest among the local people and Government of the State 
concerned which can ensure their speedy development and timely completion. (Para 29)  
  The Committee is of the view that Ministry of tou rism should concentrate on promoting 
accommodation for the domestic tourists who usually prefer affordable and safe accommodation 
rather than the costly star hotels. The Committee, therefore, recommends that budget hotels 
aimed at the domestic tourists should also be given  priority by the Ministry of Tourism and 
accordingly all the promotional measures and tax be nefits should also to be extended to the 
budget hotels and restaurants also. (Para 30)  
  The Committee notes that huge amount is pending w ith various State Governments and 
they are yet to complete the projects and submit th e utilization certificates. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should pursue with the State Governments to identify 
the reasons for delay of each of the projects and i f it is found that the project is not feasible due 
to one or the other reasons, alternate projects may  be allowed for the States. The Committee 
also recommends that in future projects may be allo wed only after getting all the necessary 
clearance from various agencies. 
  (Para 33)  
  The Committee also pointed out that in many cases  the projects are approved without 
doing adequate home work and later on abandoned mid way, because of functional and 
operational difficulties. The Committee noted that in certain cases even 80 per cent of the total 
sanctioned amount was released to the project, but later on it was abandoned due to unknown 
reasons. This is because of poor planning and imple mentation methodology adopted by the 
ministry while sanctioning the projects. The Committee in this respect is of the view that before 
a project is approved by the ministry, they should ensure the feasibility of the project and get all 
the necessary clearances from other related agencies before releasing the money.            (Para 34)  

  The Committee conveys its displeasure over the wa y the projects are sanctioned and 
implemented by the Ministry where there are lots of  wastages of money and manpower. Land 
related issues and environmental clearances should be dealt with in order to ensure a smooth 
implementation and completion of the projects. (Para 35)  
  The Committee is constrained to say that the work  Ajanta-Ellora Phase-II which was 
started in in 2003-04, is yet to the completed. It appears that the project progress has not been 
monitored properly and expected obstacle in its com pletion could not be identified. Now the 
project is scheduled to be completed by June 2010. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of Culture for timely completion of its project.  
(Para 37)  
DOMESTIC CAMPAIGN 
  The Committee notes that out of Rs.54 crore appro ved for domestic campaign for the year 
2009-10, only an amount of Rs. 16.11 crore was expected to be utilized till December. It presents 
a very dismal state of affairs. The Committee finds  that the actual utilization, in the domestic 
tourism promotion measures up to the month of Febru ary 2010, is only 30 per cent of the 
budgetary provision during 2009-10 and how the rema ining funds would be utilized within a 
month in a suitable and effective manner, is not kn own. It seems that the Ministry’s main focus 
is on overseas campaigning and has neglected the domestic tourism promotion activities. It must 
be noted that domestic tourism has great importance  as a large number of people are visiting 
places in connection with marriage, pilgrimage and other such occasions where overtly or 
covertly tourism is promoted. The Committee feels that there is need to tap the existing domestic 
market by informing domestic travelers through sust ained campaigning. The Committee 
recommends that the promotion of domestic tourists should be the main agenda of the Ministry 
of Tourism as compared to the domestic tourists, th e number of foreign tourists is very 
miniscule. The State Governments must also be involved in the process. The domestic campaign 
should also concentrate on the facilities etc. avai lable at major tourist spots and the means and 
modes of transportation to reach those places. The malpractices and misleading propaganda of 
touts and middlemen at tourist place also be brought out through domestic campaigns. 
(Para 43)  
OVERSEAS CAMPAIGN 
  The Committee notes that the Incredible India cam paign launched abroad has brought in 
foreign tourists to various parts of country. This has also helped tourist and gained popularity 
amongst travellers all over the world. The Committe e recommends that allocation made under 
this head should be utilized scrupulously for conti nuing the overseas campaign so that more 
foreign tourists are attracted and in turn help foreign exchange earnings. (Para 52)  
  India also, like China and USA, need to do a lot like development of infrastructure at the 
tourists places, etc. Private participation needs to be encouraged. (Para 53)  
  The Committee expresses its serious concern for o ver sensitizing even local issues which 
hampers the tourism promotion. The Committee critic izes the way in which the terrorist 
attacks, the swine flu and stray cases of harassmen t of foreign tourists etc, were handled, had 
quite an adverse impact over the image of India abr oad. The committee is of the view that the 

Ministry should take necessary steps in ensuring th at media should not unnecessarily create 
panic. 
(Para 54)  
TRAINING 
  The Committee is not satisfied with the efforts m ade by the Ministry regarding human 
resource development. The Government has not made s ufficient plan outlay under the head 
‘assistance for manpower training’. In the year 200 9-10, an amount of Rs. 100.70 crore was 
allocated. For the 2010-11 there is negligible increase in the plan outlay i.e. Rs. 102.50 crore. The 
Committee is constrained to note that up to Februar y 2010, ones 64% of plan outlay is likely to 
be utilized. Government have plans to set up new IHM in various parts of the country. However, 
the Committee has not been informed whether any target has been fixed for completion of these 
institutes. The Committee feels that the huge shortage of about 1.9 lakhs can not be met only by 
the Government’s initiatives alone. The Committee r ecommends that the universities under the 
UGC and the technical institutions under AICTE may be encouraged to open courses on 
hospitality industry and necessary financial assist ance for infrastructural and other required 
facilities may be extended by the Ministry of Touri sm. They should be come out with ambitious 
courses in coordination with the hospitality indust ry which will provide employability to those 
opting for the courses in those universities and te chnical institutions. External support may be 
extended by the Ministry of Tourism to these agenci es as they have the men and material for 
conducting quality courses.                                                                                                      (Para 63)  
TOURIST GUIDES 
  The Committee is concerned that with a huge manpo wer and resources within the 
country, it seems the will to facilitate tourist visiting India is lacking on the part of Government. 
Tourism Sector cannot grow without the support of g uides. Often foreign visitors complain of 
lack of guides as they are made to suffer from the hands of touts. With thousands of historical 
places and monuments all over the country, there is  need to have interpretation centres from 
where tourists can obtain all information regarding a particular site. 
  The Committee feels that in consultation with UGC  and AICTE, the Ministry should 
devise short duration courses to overcome the short age of tourists guides. Further, foreign 
language courses should also be encouraged by intro ducing suitable schemes in colleges and 
educational institutions. The Ministry of Tourism should also come forward to provide financial 
assistance to those institutions and universities f or starting foreign language courses/imparting 
training in foreign languages.

REPORT  
  Roads have an important role in the economic deve lopment of a country. India has a vast road network  of 3.62 
million km. that consists of Expressways, National Highways, State Highways, major district roads, other district roads 
and village roads. The National Highways and the St ate Highways together account for 2,04,000 kms. The  length of 
National Highways network at present is 70,934 kms.  constituting about 2 per cent of the total road ne twork in the 
country and carrying about 40 per cent of the total  traffic across the length and breadth of the count ry. Between 2001-
02 and 2005-06 the number of vehicles had grown at an average pace of 10 per cent per annum and consequently traffic 
on the roads has increased at 7 -10 per cent per an num. The share of roads in total traffic has been g rowing from 13.8 
per cent of freight traffic and 15.4 per cent of th e passenger traffic in 1950-51 to 60 per cent of fr eight traffic and 87.4 
per cent of passenger traffic respectively by the end of 2005-06. 
2.  This unprecedented growth of road traffic, call s for a massive expansion and improvement of the road network in 
the country. This would require a massive infusion of funds supported by efficient mechanisms and trained manpower. 
Historically in India, investments in roads, especi ally highways, were mainly made by the Government b ecause of the 
large volume of resources required, long gestation period of projects, uncertain returns and various a ssociated 
externalities. But in recent times, the private sec tor has been actively involved in the development a nd maintenance of 
the National Highways. 
3.  The Ministry has formulated policy guidelines t o encourage private sector participation in the hig hway sector, 
besides providing several incentives such as tax ex emptions and duty free import of road building equi pment and 
machinery. Model Concession Agreements have also been finalized for major road projects, under PPP model. 
4.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is basically responsible for the construction and main tenance of 
National Highways (NH), administration of Motor Veh icle Act and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, formulat ion of 
broad policies relating to road transport, environmental issues relating to vehicular movements, automotive norms, etc. 
besides making arrangements for movements of vehicular traffic with neighbouring countries. 
5.  The development and maintenance of National Hig hways are being done on agency basis mainly by the National 
Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Wo rks Departments (PWDs) and the Border Roads Organiz ation. 
Out of the total length of 70,934 km of National Hi ghways, 42,598 km is with the State Public Works De partments 
(State PWDs), 20,666 km with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and 3,892 km with the Bor der Road 
Organization. Remaining 3,778 km is yet to be entrusted to the executing agencies. 
6.  The National Highways have further been classif ied depending upon the width formation. Generally, a lane has a 
width of 3.75 metres in case of single lane and 3.5  metres in case of multi lane National Highways. Th e break-up of 
National Highways in terms of width is as under: 
  Single Lane/Intermediate lane 19,803 km. (28%) 
  Double Lane 38,006 km. (53.5%) 
  Four/Six/Eight Lane 13,125 km. (14%)

the financial year 2010-11 was considered by the  Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 22nd  March, 2010. During the meeting, the Committee too k oral 
evidence of the Secretary and other officers of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
