(5)  Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI) 
(6)  National Research Laboratory for Conservation of Cultural Property (NRLC)  
(7)  National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) 
(8)  Central Reference Library (CRL) National Resea rch Laboratory for Conservation of 
Cultural Property (NRLC) 
128.   For filling up of these posts it was decided  to institute Search- Cum- Selection procedure 
in order to induct professionals to these posts. Me anwhile, Recruitment Rules attached to these posts 
were taken up for revision in consultation with DOPT & Ministry of Law. 
129.   The post of DG, Archaeological Survey of Ind ia has since been filled up as per Search-
Curn-Selection procedure. For filling up the posts of DG, National Museum, Director, National 
Library & DG, National Archives of India is in proc ess. The Recruitment Rules for the post of 
Director, Anthropological Survey of India is under revision for institution of a Search-Cum- Selection 
procedure. The post of Director General, National M useum is being held on ‘additional charge basis’ 
by a Joint Secretary level officer from Ministry of Culture. 
130.  The Secretary while deposing before the Committee stated: 
“Sir, eight of the cultural organizations are gover nmental and 33 are autonomous......Of the 8 
governmental organizations, the most momentous deve lopment that has taken place in the last 
few months relates to the professionalization of th eir recruitment. They were all controlled by 
the UPSC. The UPSC has its strong plus points, and,  somewhere, maybe we could have a 
deviation from it. This thing of taking into accoun t the UPSC took about two to three years. 

Finally, all the posts have been taken out, and, ar e filled in or about to be filled in except the 
one, for which we seek your help as individuals and  as Members of Parliament. It is the post of 
DG, National Museum. For the post of DG of National  Archives, somebody’s name has been 
sent. Director, National Library is joining next we ek. Seventeen years after the last professional 
archeologist left the ASI, it has been managed in an adhoc  manner by the Additional Secretaries 
from the Indian Administrative Service. This has given weight to another professional coming in 
and taking over. All the eight posts except the one  of DG, National Museum are filled in. 
Despite the best search-cum-selection committee tha t was put in by flying in an Indian 
expatriate, internationally renowned in the world o f museums, we could not select a single 
person in India at present, who can be given the charge. We will go through another round. This 
is not the end of the case. As I said, only the pos t of DG, National Museum is left. So, the issue 
of headless-ness is a matter of history.” 
131.   The Committee notes that the cultural institutions in our country are in a state of 
crisis most of which have remained headless for man y years. This Committee has been pointing 
out about this from time to time. The Committee not es the efforts made by the Governments in 
appointing heads of various national institutions i n recent times. The Committee recommends 
that every effort should be made to ensure that all  the institutional heads are appointed at the 
earliest. The process further need to be streamlined and vacant post filled up on urgent basis. 
NATIONAL CULTURE POLICY  
132.  A National Committee was constituted on 11.11 .2006 for drafting the National Policy on 
Culture. The term of the Committee was extended upt o 30.06.2008. It was informed that the 
Committee met several times but the final decision is still awaited from them. The Secretary in his 
submission stated that: 
“the draft cultural policy has been submitted by te n, twelve important cultural personalities. I 
myself submitted it to my ex-Minister. I think, he rightly said.” 
133.   The Committee was informed by the Secretary that the Central Advisory Board on 
Culture passed a few directions, and at the next me eting of the Central Advisory Board, which is 
chaired by the hon. Prime Minister they would be ab le to take a view either way. There is a feeling 
that it be called a framework or a programme rather  than a policy because a policy may have a 
directional flavour in it. 
134.   The Committee notes that the Government has neither  shown any long-term vision 
nor any substantial short-term action to arrest the decay that has set in. The Ministry of Culture 
must move its wheels to generate a vision for the f uture that includes a sensible policy towards 
their missions. The Committee recommends that the N ational Culture Policy may be brought 
out at the earliest. 
ANTIQUITIES AND ART TREASURES ACT, 1972  
135.   The Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972 enacted by Parliament, came into force from 
5.4.1976. The primary purpose of the Act is to regulate the export trade in antiquities and art treasures, 
to provide for the prevention of smuggling of and f raudulent dealings in antiquities, to provide for the 
compulsory acquisition of antiquities and art treasures for preservation in public places. 

136.   Amendment of the Act has been proposed, to u pdate some provisions and make it more 
stringent and in pursuance thereto, a review of various provisions of the Antiquities and Art Treasures 
Act, 1972 is under consideration. The Secretary informed that: 
“Sir, the Antiquities Act was promulgated in 1972 t o stop certain priceless jewels or other 
jewellery from leaving India. The prologue of the A ct mentions that it was meant for stopping 
Indian treasures from going abroad. In reality, the system that was set up is said to be a little bit 
cumbersome. Every antiquity would mean to be regist ered and all that. We are told that the 
provisions of internal movement within India could be revisited and eased up in terms of 21st 
century like where instead of filing up a form phys ically, you do it by e-mail, or, you buy an e-
ticket. Right now, . there is a strong bi-polarity in our approach. On the one hand, the outgoing 
DG has given a strong suggestion for strengthening the Act in the sense of putting up physical 
inspectorate. He lacks manpower, and, so, he will ask for it. On the other hand, there is a feeling 
that while absolutely no compromise can be made abo ut antiquities leaving India, if there is a 
movement within the republic, there would be econom ic stimulus of art and antiquities, and, 
then, the republic and the people would stand to ga in. We are caught between the two view 
points, and, we may be heading for a committee disc ussion. We cannot take a unilateral view. 
DG’s part is over. He said, give me so many people, I will do the job. The Antiquities Act needs 
to be looked into. Maybe this Committee could find time and give us the benefit of its views at a 
separate session.” 
137.  The Committee is of the view that amendments in the proposed Act are the need of ho ur and it should be done in a time bound manner. The apprehension of the public who are scared to show antiquities should be removed. There should be some mechanism of one time voluntary disclosure and registration of articles as there is a boom in art 
market and with the amendment in the Act, the trade can be done within the country, lawfully 
benefitting the country.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS –– AT A GLANCE  
  The Committee underlines the need for more allocat ion to the Ministry of Culture lest 
many of its important activities should suffer. For the year 2010-11, the Ministry of Culture has 
been allocated an amount of Rs.735 crore which comes to less than 12 paise per hundred rupees 
being spent under the General Budget. However, the Committee is surprised to find that during 
the first three years of the XI Five Year Plan, the  Ministry as in the past, has not been able to 
utilize even the reduced allocation. Underutilizati on of funds by the Ministry of Culture is a 
recurring phenomena year after year. During the yea r 2009-10 the allocation of Rs.700 crore 
was reduced to Rs.630.00 crore at RE stage, however , the Ministry could utilize only an amount 
of Rs.533.40 crore. The Committee recommends that t he Ministry should identify the 
bottlenecks and make corrective measures to utilize  the allocations as per the norms laid down 
for the purpose.                                                                                                                (Para 12)  
  The Committee notes the comments of the Ministry of Finance. However, the Ministry of 
Finance/Planning Commission has not offered any sol ution to the problem of the Ministry of 
Culture which the Committee still appreciates. The Committee deplores the “one size fits all” 
attitude of the Ministry of Finance and recommends that the non-utilization of funds due to the 
hostile weather and season may be given a special s tatus to ensure that allocation is not reduced 
at RE stage. Till there is no respite on this accou nt, the Ministry of Culture will have to make 
efforts to maximize its expenditure, before the review of the RE allocation begins. (Para 16)  
  The Ministry should also explore new methodology for conservation and preservation with 
the help of Scientists/Universities which can be do ne in all weather conditions. The Committee 
observes that the fund allocated to ASI need to be given a special status to make it non-lapsable. (Para 17)  
  The Committee once again recommends to the Minist ry of Finance and the Planning 
Commission to understand the needs of the instituti ons working under the Ministry of Culture 
and the limitations of those institutions to spend the money during the first six months of the 
financial year. (Para 18)  
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
  The Committee notes various activities undertaken  by ASI in the field of Culture and 
appreciates the efforts of ASI. (Para 24)  
  The Committee notes the excavation work in variou s places and recommends that every 
care be taken to ensure that the time schedule pres cribed for each of the excavation work is 
adhered.     (Para 29)  
  The Committee recommends that ASI should explore new scientific methods to preserve 
and conserve the heritage sites. The major research and scientific institutions may be roped in to 
explore newer technology and scientific knowledge for preservation and conservation of heritage 
sites.      (Para 30)  
CULTURAL AWARENESS PROGRAMME 
  The Committee is of the view that there is a need  for publications in archaeology for 
general awareness in all the major Indian languages , besides some foreign languages. These 
publications should aim at creating interest in the  public about our ancient monuments and 

archaeological sites as well the importance of pres erving these as our cultural heritage. Such 
awareness in the general public would facilitate better protection/maintenance of these sites. (Para 32)  
  Further, there is need for generating interest am ongst general public, specially children, 
by putting some special programme such as puppet sh ow, documentary etc. Moreover, the 
display boards should be made bilingual and it shou ld have all the relevant information about a 
particular site. Brochures should be made available  in local language also. NGOs/College 
students may also be roped in to act as volunteers/guides to ensure the local participation. (Para 33)  
  The Committee hopes that upgradation/ modernizati on of all site museums will be 
completed in time.   (Para 35)  
  The Committee notes the steps taken by the ASI in  involving school children in their effort 
to popularize and preserve our monuments. The Commi ttee recommends that the local 
community and the students of local colleges and ed ucational institutions may also be involved 
in the various activities/efforts of ASI. (Para 37)  
FUND ALLOCATION FOR ASI 
  The Committee notes that inspite of cuts/reductio ns in all the heads, ASI was provided 
with increased allocation from the scarce resources  to meet their expenditure. However, the 
Committee is concerned to note that ASI was able to  incur expenditure only to the tune of Rs. 
110.07 crore. ASI should ensure their spending of f unds in an effective way so that the entire 
allocated fund is utilized within the stipulated ti me frame specified. The Committee may be 
apprised about the reasons for non-utilization of funds. (Para 40)  
  During the Commonwealth Games it is anticipated t hat a large number of tourists would 
visit various monuments in and around Delhi under t he protection of ASI. There is a need for 
common entry ticketing system alongwith availabilit y of tickets on Internet. The Committee 
feels that unifying the entry system to the various  monuments under the control of ASI as well 
as the tourists booking their entry tickets. throug h Internet would be of great help to tourist. 
The common entry ticket system need to be introduce d before the Commonwealth Games 2010. 
The Committee recommends that the ASI should coordi nate with the Ministry of Tourism to 
ensure that the tourists had a pleasant and hassle free experience during their visit to various 
monuments. The Committee further recommends that cl eanliness and other basic facilities may 
be ensured at all the monuments.   
 
PROTECTION OF MONUMENTS 
  The Committee also agrees in-principle to such a convergence between the Centre and 
States as far as development and protection of our ancient heritage is concerned. Under the 
existing system, due to lack of sharing and close c oordination there is complete confusion 
between ASI and the States Archaeology Departments.  As a result, hundreds of our heritage 
sites are either not identified & notified and have  been demolished or encroached upon. Such a 
sharing would, the Committee feels, go a long way i n protecting, pressing and developing our 
ancient sites.                                                                                                                         (Para 44)  
  The Committee is concerned at the lack of coordin ation between the Central and State 
Governments. So much so, the ASI was not aware of t he steps taken by the State Governments 
to protect their monuments. The monuments under the  control of State Governments also need 

to be preserved and protected. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Culture should 
ensure that the monuments under the control of Stat e Governments are also protected and 
maintained. If necessary, the Ministry should also explore the possibility of giving adequate 
finance to the State authorities in this regard. Th e Committee is of the view that Government 
needs to take effective steps to coordinate and fac ilitate the monitoring of protection of 
monuments by State Governments.    
STAFF STRENGTH OF ASI 
The Committee is of the view that ASI has spread it self thin and a severe shortage of technical 
personnel has hamstrung the conservation efforts. T he Committee will like to invite the 
attention to the recommendation of the R.N. Mirdha Committee that a minimum of 9,000 
monument attendants would be needed to provide secu rity to the existing structures. The 
Government of India needs to rethink its ‘fence and forget’ approach towards the monuments. (Para 49)  
  The shortage of staff and monument attendants is a serious problem affecting the safety, 
security and upkeep of various monuments adversely. The monuments need to be protected just 
like any other assets of nation. The Committee, the refore, recommends that the Government 
should make efforts on a war footing to ensure that  staff strength as recommended by various 
Committees may be increased and personnel are posted at the earliest. (Para 50)  
  The Committee has come to know that there are hun dreds of attendants who are 
protecting the monuments for 20 years or more, have  not been regularized till date. As a result, 
their basic pay is static and no other allowances a re being paid to them. It is also learnt that 
some of them had gone to Court, but could not get any relief. It is a strange situation when there 
is a huge backlog at different levels including that of monument attendants, yet the existing staff 
are not being adjusted. The Committee, therefore, s trongly recommends that Ministry of 
Culture should adopt humanitarian approach and take steps to increase their wages taking into 
account their length of service and rate of inflation.   
 
  The current framework operates at two levels - Ce ntral, that looks after nationally 
important monuments, and the State-level that is re sponsible for State protected monuments. 
There is an urgent need of activating a third level  of institutional and legal arrangement 
involving local bodies and all these levels need to  work with a very close coordination and well 
defined partnership, legal, financial, etc..    
  The Committee recommends that for preservation of  our monuments activities should be 
decentralized. The historical monuments can be bett er protected by the involvement of local 
people. The Ministry should come out with a decentr alized and integrated mechanism that 
would fill the gaps existing today in this regard. The Committee has already expressed its 
serious reservation about the proposed National Heritage Commission that it will not be able to 
address the major issues currently faced in identif ying, developing, protecting, etc. of our rich 
heritage scattered all over the country from Delhi to Talukas and remote villages. (Para 53)  
HORTICULTURE BRANCH OF ASI 
  The Committee was informed that the proposal for restructuring the Archaeological 
Survey of India has been prepared as per the guidelines of Department of Personnel & Training 
and Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure taking into account the requirements of 
each Wing/Branch of the Archaeological Survey of In dia including Horticulture Wing. The 
proposal has been submitted to the Ministry of Cult ure for further action in the matter. The 

Committee is constrained to note that the proposal for restructuring of the Horticultural Branch 
is pending for a long time and till date no decisio n has been taken. The Committee recommends 
that the Government should take speedy action on th e proposal of restructuring of Horticulture 
Branch of ASI so that they can take additional activities. (Para 57)  
  The Committee realizes the need for green environ ment and gardens around the 
monuments. The Committee notes that there is severe  shortage of gardeners and posts need to 
be filled up. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Ministry of Culture should take 
immediate steps to fill up the vacant posts. (Para 58)  
ENCROACHMENTS AND REHABILITATION 
  The Committee notes that despite there being stri ct rules under the Ancient Monuments 
and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958, the problem of encroachment of monuments 
could not be checked. The Committee was informed that the 35 monuments, all managed by the 
Central Government, could not be traced. Delhi, the  headquarters of Archeological Survey of 
India, tops the list with 12 untraceable monuments.  They now exist only in memory and in 
history books. The Committee would like to invite t he attention of the Government to the plight 
of the older Forts in the country. Many of those Fo rts are made up of dry sandstone on 
foundations of clay, sand and rock. These forts are  facing the problem of encroachments also. 
These forts are ill-maintained and in a dilapidated  condition. The growth of tourism and the 
large number of visitors are putting unbearable pre ssure on the structures. One example is the 
Jaisalmer Fort also known as ‘ Sonar Qila’ or ‘Jewel of Desert ’ which is reported to have been 
listed among the most endangered sites of the World  Monuments Fund. It is reported, that the 
waste water has seeped through decayed drains and penetrated the walls of the Fort resulting in 
cracks in various structures of the Fort. The Fort is also facing the problem of encroachment. (Para 61)  
  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Min istry of Culture should take up the 
matter with the concerned State Governments and oth er authorities to ensure that the Forts 
which are part of our cultural heritage are not fur ther damaged due to human action. The 
Committee also recommends that the Ministry should take effective steps to protect the forts 
from neglect and destruction.   
 
  The Committee feels that since in the removal of encroachment, the major role has to be 
played by the State Government, their stake has to be properly recognized. The Ministry should 
initiate consultation with State Government and wor k out a plan for rehabilitation. Financial 
assistance for heritage protection needs to be increased. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
for a separate allocation for dealing with illegal encroachments in ASI monuments and 
rehabilitation to solve this perennial problem. (Para 63)  
NATIONAL MISSION ON MONUMENTS AND ANTIQUITIES 
  The Committee appreciates the setting up of Natio nal Mission on Monuments and 
Antiquities which will bring in record all the cult ural and heritage properties and antiquities 
available in the country. The documentation of the heritage sites and antiquities is a gigantic 
task for which the Government of India have sanctio ned a budgetary allocation of Rs.90 crore 
and the project has to be completed within a period  of five years from 2007-12. The Committee, 
in view of urgency of the work, calls up the Minist ry to complete the work in a time bound way 
and make available more funds if required for the p urpose. The Committee is also of the view 
that Mission has to do a huge task which cannot be completed without the involvement of 

general public. The Committee recommends that Gover nment should take steps to sensitize the 
masses and take assistance of the NGO already working in this area.  (Para 72)  
ZONAL CULTURAL CENTRES (ZCC) 
  The Committee notes the efforts of Zonal Cultural  Centres in preserving the Indian 
culture. However, the Committee is not happy that p lan allocation of Rs.14 crore for the year 
2009-10 was reduced to Rs.12.75 crore at RE stage. Such reduction are not unusual but in cash 
starved Department, efforts should be to utilize th e plan outlay for some other similar purpose, 
if organizing folk dance festival in Delhi was not possible. The Committee feels that there need 
to be more publicity of the events being organized by Zonal Cultural Centres. Without reaching 
the masses, the Zonal Cultural Centres cannot achie ve their objectives. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that concerted efforts should  be made for publicity of the events at 
school and college levels also. (Para 75)  
NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA 
  The Committee notes the role of the three Akademi s, viz . Sangeet Natak Akademi, Lalit 
Kala Akademi and Sahitya Akademi and National Schoo l of Drama in promotion of literary, 
visual and performing arts. However, the Committee is constrained to note that there has been 
lack of consistency in the matter of utilization of plan outlays in these Akademis during the year 
2009-10. An amount of Rs.13.10 crore was provided f or Sangeet Natak Akademi and was 
reduced to Rs.12.2 crore at RE stage. In the case of Lalit Kala Academy an amount of Rs.6 crore 
was reduced to Rs.1.5 crore at RE stage for which n o reasons have been given. An amount of 
Rs.10.5 crore allocated at BE 2009-10 was reduced t o Rs.6.30 crore at RE stage on account of 
slow pace of expenditure incurred in the first two quarters of the financial year. The Committee 
would like to know the actual reasons of non-utilization of funds by these Akademis and also the 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should have proactive approach while assessing the 
schemes to be carried out by the Societies during t he financial year, so that there is no last-
minute change which may result in non-utilization of plan outlays.   
 
  The Committee is of the view that Sangeet Natak A kademi has to do much more and reach 
the general public through mass media. Further, the re is need for innovative efforts so that the 
reach of Sangeet Natak Akademi is widened. The Committee hopes that Lalit Kala Akademi will 
be able to improve its infrastructural facilities before the Commonwealth Games. Further, more 
regional centres should be established with focus o n more art galleries. The Committee hopes 
that with the increased allocation, Sahitya Akademi  would be able to do its job effectively. 
However, there is need to set up more bookshops and  mobile vans so that the efforts of Sahitya 
Akademi reaches the masses. Mobile vans should visi t various schools, residential areas, office 
complex etc. to reach to the general public.    
INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL CENTRE FOR THE ARTS (IGNCA) 
  The Committee notes the efforts made by IGNCA in promoting the activities under its 
control. The Committee recommends that there is nee d to set up more sub-centers in various 
parts of country.    (Para 84) 
NATIONAL GALLERY OF MODERN ART 
  The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) is a un ique institute of the country which 
represents the evolution and pictorial transformati on in the visual arts in India over the last 
century. However, the Committee is not happy over t he utilization of plan allocation by the 

NGMA. The amount of Rs.7 crore provided in BE 2009-10 was reduced significantly at RE stage 
to Rs.5.3 crore, on account of slow pace of expenditure incurred by NGMA. Committee finds the 
reason given for underutilization of funds ambiguous. The Committee notes that new building in 
New Delhi is under construction and hopes that it w ill be completed at the earliest. Further, the 
Committee is of the view that safety of the article s kept in the Museum is of paramount 
importance. The Committee recommends that necessary  fund may be provided for installing 
latest security gadgets to beef up the security of the Museum.    
THE ASIATIC SOCIETY, KOLKATA 
  The Asiatic Society undertakes activities connect ed with conservation of Art objects, 
sculptures and manuscripts, augmentation of researc h programmes, strengthening of 
publication activities, computerization of library activities etc. However, the Committee fails to 
understand as to why the work for improvement and u pgradation of the institution was not 
taken up as a result of which the amount of Rs.21 c rore allocated to the Asiatic Society was 
reduced to Rs.10.5 crore. The Committee hopes that they would be able to utilize the plan outlay 
optimally during the year 2010-11.   
 
NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA 
  The Committee notes that National Archives of Ind ia has highly competent professionals 
in the field of Archives record management, conserv ation, reprography and other related fields 
of Archival Science. The National Archives has grea t task before it of managing records. The 
Committee is also of the view that the National Arc hives should conduct regular courses for the 
employees of government offices and if possible dep ute staff from its organization to assist 
various offices to maintain record in a better way.  However, the Committee notes that the plan 
outlay of Rs.4.50 crore made in BE 2009-10 was redu ced to Rs.3.75 crore at RE stage. Again an 
amount of Rs.5.00 crore has been provided in BE 201 0-11. The Committee feels that there is 
some sort of inconsistency in the planning which has resulted in fluctuation of plan outlay at BE 
and RE stages which can affect the functioning and activities of the National Archives of India. (Para 95)  
MUSEUMS 
  The Committee notes that India has a number of Mu seums under its control, both 
Government and private. The allocations to the Muse ums is enough as is evident from the 
utilisation of allocation under Museum head. In 2009-10, allocation of Rs. 72.36 crore was made. 
The actual expenditure upto 31st March, 2010 is Rs.  71.50 crore. However, there is need for 
detailed pamphlets listing numerous exhibitions, IM AX and Space Shows, optional audio tours 
for an extra fee, special lectures and the Restaura nts which can create interest in the minds of 
people. (Para 104)  
  There is also need to review the timings of the M useum which should be extended in 
evening hours keeping in view that in most part of India, days are very hot. During School 
vacations, time should be extended so that children can visit it in the evenings with their parents. (Para 105)  
  Further, Security should be strengthened in all t he museums. The punishment for doing 
any damage to the museum should be explicitly displayed at all the prominent places. (Para 106)  
  More than that India’s brilliant IT and engineeri ng brains could be garnered to design 
new and exciting exhibits, marking the beginning of  transforming museums into “edutainment” 
destinations.    (Para 107)  

LIBRARIES 
  The Committee notes that the Central Secretariat Library with a huge depository of books 
and volumes are not accessible to the common public  due to security reasons. The Committee 
recommends that the Central Secretariat Library may  be moved out of the high security area 
and housed at a place where the researchers, studen ts, academician and general public can 
access it. The Ministry of Culture may also explore the possibility of constructing a new campus 
for the Central Secretariat Library. (Para 112)  
  The allocation to the Public Libraries was Rs. 40 .62 crore in the year 2009-10. The 
expenditure upto 31st March 2010 is Rs 40.13 crore.  The Committee is of the view that the 
Government should provide more funds to the Librari es through Ministry of Culture, if it can 
be utilised by them. However, there need to be some  improvement as such the catalogue of the 
libraries should be available on internet. The Computers and softwares installed in the libraries 
should be in working conditions all the time so tha t readers are not put to inconvenience. The 
concept of community libraries should be explored a nd they should be promoted with wide 
publicity.  (Para 120)  
  The Committee at the same time observed that wher ever large collections did exist, they 
were not fully used because of rigid rules. Library  users were not trusted and were asked 
security deposit, which every library users may not afford. (Para 121)  
PROJECT/SCHEMES FOR PROMOTION OF ART AND CULTURE FOR NORTH-EAST

REPORT  
  Civil Aviation sector is one of the major sectors  which have seen remarkable growth in the 
recent past. The economic melt down and increased A TF , prices have had some negative impact on 
civil aviation during the last year, but the sector  was able to regain some of its lost ground. India has 
become the ninth largest civil aviation market in t he world as well as major aviation hub in the Asia 
Pacific market, which is having 647 million air passengers this year. The country is expecting to reach 
500 million passengers in 2030 and in the coming th ree to five years it will reach the target of 200 
million passengers. Due to the open sky policy and liberalization the number of aircraft has increased  
manifold in recent years. As such the civil aviation sector has become a much happening one. 
2.  The Ministry of Civil Aviation is responsible f or the formulation of national policies and 
programmes for the development and regulation of ci vil aviation in the country and for devising and 
implementing schemes for orderly growth and expansi on of civil air transport. Its functions also 
extend to overseeing the provision of airport facil ities, air traffic services, carriage of passengers  and 
goods by air, safeguarding civil aviation operation s, regulation of air transport services, licensing of 
aerodromes, air carriers, pilots and aircraft maintenance engineers. In addition to framing policies, the 
Ministry provides guidance to the organizations in the implementation of policy guidelines. 
3.  The Ministry of Civil Aviation has the followin g organizations under its administrative control:–

Chennai airport will be completed by January, 2011 while the work on Kolkata airport will be 
completed by May, 2011. Adequate funds had been provided for these mega projects in the budget for 
2010-2011. The Committee was also informed that the  modernization and upgradation works at 35 
non-metro airports were progressing as per schedule . Chairman, AAI while deposing before the

Jabalpur airport is in limbo for so many years. The  Committee desires that the AAI should 
pursue the allocation of land for development of Ja balpur airport with the State Government. 
The Committee recommends that every effort should b e made to operationalize the night 
landing system and expansion of the runway of the J abalpur airport. The Committee also 
desires that the development work of Kanpur airport should be taken up on priority so that this 
industrial town is also included in the aviation map of the country. The Committee feels that the 
development of Bihta airfield is the need of hour t o ease the burden of Patna airport since there 
is little scope for expansion of runway at Patna ai rport. The Committee is of the opinion that 
unused airports/airstrips should also be developed in consultation with State Governments as 
provision of air connectivity should not be restricted to major cities only. It was further brought 
to the notice of the Committee that various tourist destinations of the country lack airstrips even 
for helicopter services. Thekkady and Bekal in Kera la are two such destinations. The AAI 
should explore the possibility of constructing airs trips at these places to boost the tourism 
potential of these areas.

ROLE  OF  CIVIL  AVIATION  IN  PROMOTION  OF  TOURISM  
76.  Aviation sector plays an important role in pro motion of tourism in the country. Provision of 
Airport infrastructure and uninterrupted air connec tivity play a vital role in bringing more and more 
places into the tourism map of the country. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry o f 
Civil Aviation can play an anchor role in promoting  such unexplored tourist places with the 
coordination of State Governments, tourism department and local bodies by providing requisite 

airport infrastructure. Places in North East and Le h region could be easily accessible by air 
rather than a taxing road journey. The Committee fe els that the Ministry should strengthen the 
airport infrastructure and enhance air services to these areas. The Committee came to know 
about the hardship faced by Government employees in  getting tickets under L T80 scheme for 
air travel using the Leave Travel Concession. Limit ed availability of seats has made getting 
confirmed tickets under this scheme a hard proposal . The Committee feels that NACIL should 
take steps to increase the number of seats under the category to alleviate the present hardship of 
getting tickets under the LT80 scheme. The Committe e is of the opinion that special tourist 
packages for air travel should be made available region-wise to cater the needs of air travellers.  
GENERAL  OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS  
77.  The Committee on scrutinizing of budget papers of M inistry of Civil Aviation finds that 
the over all performance of the Ministry during the  last year has been almost satisfactory. The 
Committee feels that strengthening of aviation infrastructure, inculcating corporate governance 
in NACIL, promotion of helicopter tourism, strength ening and restructuring of DGCA and 
BCAS, empowering AAI and providing it a level playi ng field in development and 
modernization of airports, etc. are some of the major areas where the Ministry has to take some 
initiatives. Shortage of pilots, Air Traffic Contro llers, Aerodrome Inspectors, Helicopter 
inspectors is also major cause of concern. The Comm ittee feels that unless the Ministry 
addresses these issues with a sense of urgency, it cannot keep the present momentum of the 
industry for long. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry will take at the necessary 
steps to meet shortage of man power so that the mis match in demand and supply in aviation 
market is addressed successfully. The Committee further hopes that the Ministry will take more 
steps to make air travel an affordable, reliable and safe one.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS –– AT A GLANCE  
ANNUAL  PLAN  2009-10 
  The Committee notes that the Ministry was able to  expend the allocations made during 
2009-10 near to cent per cent. The expenditure patt ern of the Ministry has seen a remarkable 
improvement as compared to the previous years. The Committee hopes that the spending 
pattern of the Ministry in 2009-10 will become a be nch mark for them and hopes that the 
Ministry will be in a position to repeat the performance in this year also. (Para 8)  
ANNUAL  PLAN  FOR  2010-11 
  The Committee after examining the allocations for  2010-11 finds that Rs. 85 crore has 
been allocated under Non-Plan which is merely Rs. 1 0 crore more than that of the allocation in 
2009-10. The Committee feels that the allocation is  inadequate considering the functioning and 
responsibilities discharged by various offices unde r the Ministry of Civil Aviation. The 
Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry shoul d persuade the Planning Commission to 
allocate more funds under this head at RE stage, so  that, civil aviation sector does not suffer for 
want of funds. The Committee hopes that the Ministr y would be in a position to expend the 
enhanced allocation under plan head judiciously and optimally during 2010-11. (Para 13)  
NATIONAL  AVIATION  COMPANY  OF  INDIA  LIMITED 
  The Committee feels that the NACIL has to put its  act together as early as possible for 
reclaiming its ‘maharaja’ status. The Committee is of the opinion that NACIL has to be careful 
to ensure that the merger related issues not make a ny negative impact on its growth. The 
Committee feels that the Government should give more autonomy to this PSU and not impose its 
decisions on NACIL. The Committee finds that NACIL still needs some aggressive marketing 
and promotional strategies to strengthen its presen ce in domestic and international markets. 
The Committee hopes that with the induction of new aircrafts NACIL should be in a position to 
expand its air services to the length and breadth o f the country. The international connectivity 
from Guwahati and Srinagar needs to be reviewed and adequate actions may be taken. (Para 21)  
  The Committee also feels that the NACIL should re visit the underutilized bilaterals signed 
in the past and try to add more services with the new aircrafts. (Para 22)  
  The Committee is of the opinion that the performa nce of Air India Express in the low cost 
carrier market is not up to expected levels. The Co mmittee feels that NACIL should take giant 
steps to gain more market share in this market also. (Para 23)  
  The Committee had examined the issues of the merg er of Indian Airlines and Air India 
and made certain recommendations in its 151st Repor t. However, the response of the 
Government is still awaited. The Committee recommen ds that all the merger related issues 
should be settled according to the recommendations of the Parliamentary Committee. The 
Committee hopes that the NACIL will come out of the merger related issues in the coming years 
and produce the required results to establish the NACIL as leader in civil aviation market. (Para 24)  
AIRPORTS  AUTHORITY  OF  INDIA  (AAI) 
  The Committee notes that AAI has been able to uti lize around 95% of the revised 
estimates for the year 2009-10. The Committee, whil e appreciating the commitment of AAI in 
developing airport infrastructure and other facilit ies in the country, feels that the potential and 

expertise available with mini-navratna PSU is not b eing fully utilized. The Committee feels that 
with the highly trained and experienced manpower, t he AAI can give tough competition to the 
private airport developers subject to financial and  other operational autonomy available to 
them. The Committee hopes that the AAI will perform in the coming year true to its potential. (Para 31)  
ELECTRONICS 
  The Committee finds that in view of the ever incr easing number of flights in the fully 
operational airports as also more and more airports  being opened, need for having modern 
landing/take off equipments with accurate precision  has become of utmost importance. The 
Committee is of the view that GAGAN project, as usu ally happens, should not be allowed to 
languish; it should be completed by its target date i.e. June 2013. (Para 38)  
  Similarly, procurement of auto systems, surveilla nce and ancillary equipments, electronics 
and ground safety system should be done on time as these constitute important aspects of 
airports functioning.   (Para 39)  
KOLKATA  AND  CHENNAI  AIRPORTS 
  It was brought to the notice of the Committee tha t certain airports such as Jabalpur, 
Kanpur, Bihta etc. are in dire need of various deve lopmental activities. The modernization of 
Jabalpur airport is in limbo for so many years. The  Committee desires that the AAI should 
pursue the allocation of land for development of Ja balpur airport with the State government. 
The Committee recommends that every effort should b e made to operationalize the night 
landing system and expansion of the runway of the J abalpur airport. The Committee also 
desires that the development work of Kanpur airport should be taken up on priority so that this 
industrial town is also included in the aviation map of the country. The Committee feels that the 
development of Bihta airfield is the need of hour t o ease the burden of Patna airport since there 
is little scope for expansion of runway at Patna ai rport. The Committee is of the opinion that 
unused airports/airstrips should also be developed in consultation with State governments as 
provision of air connectivity should not be restricted to major cities only. It was further brought 
to the notice of the Committee that various tourist destinations of the country lack airstrips even 
for helicopter services. Thekkady and Bekal in Kera la are two such destinations. The AAI 
should explore the possibility of constructing airs trips at these places to boost the tourism 
potential of these areas. (Para 41)  
SCHEMES  UNDERTAKEN  IN  NORTH  EASTERN  REGION 
  The Committee feels that the airports in North-Ea stern Region need more attention from 
the AAI. Development of airports in Guwahati, Dibru garh and Teju should be given due 
consideration for improvement of facilities at these airports. (Para 46)  
PAWAN  HANS  HELICOPTERS  LIMITED 
  The Committee observes that Pawan Hans Helicopter  Limited has performed reasonably 
well in the last year without having additional man  power and capacity addition. The fleet 
serviceability has improved from 66% in 2006-07 to 83% in 2009-10. The operating profit has 
remarkably increased from mere Rs.2.78 crore in 200 6-07 to Rs. 34.00 crore in 2009-10. The 
Committee appreciates the performance of Pawan Hans  Helicopters Limited despite the fact 
that the overall performance of helicopter industry  has not been good. The Committee hopes 

that PHHL will keep up with this performance and wi ll not be complacent in future. The 
Committee expects a major role from the reliable he licopter service provider during the 
Commonwealth Games 2010, Delhi for a better connectivity to tourists and business community 
and also for emergency/disaster management. The Com mittee is of the opinion that PHHL 
should lend their hands in promotion of unexplored tourist destinations by expanding their 
commercial operations to such places in consultation with AAI. 
(Para 51)  
HOTEL CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED 
  The Committee feels that the handing over of Cent aur Lake View Hotel, Srinagar and 
Chefair Flight Catering, Mumbai to professionals on  Management Contract will strengthen the 
infrastructure and performance of these units. The Committee is of the opinion that Centaur 
Lake View Hotel, Srinagar requires much needed face lift and renovation to attract more 
domestic and international tourists to the valley. The Government has offered certain benefits to 
hospitality sector in connection with the Commonwea lth Games 2010. The Committee 
recommends that Government should explore the possi bility of extending some financial 
assistance to HCI for the renovation of Centaur Hotel, Delhi Airport.   
 
INDIRA  GANDHI  RASHTRIYA  URAN AKADEMI 
  The Committee feels that IGRUA being the pioneer pilot training institute plays a major 
role in the country’s requirement of pilots. The Co mmittee hopes that handing over its 
management to professionals has some positive effec ts on its performance. The Committee is of 
the opinion that after the modernization, IGRUA should be in a position to meet the shortage of 
trained manpower in the aviation industry adequately. (Para 62)  
DIRECTORATE  GENERAL  OF  CIVIL  AVIATION 
  The Committee notes that against Rs. 2 crore plan  outlay in 2008-09, the DGCA has been 
allocated Rs.86 crores in 2010-11. This manifold in crease in the allocation is in keeping with the 
need for strengthening of this aviation regulatory body in the country. The Committee hopes 
that the proposed Safety Programme will be develope d as per the schedule, so that airlines and 
airports follow the uniform safety programmes serio usly. The Committee hopes that long 
pending construction of new building for DGCA will get its final shape as shortcomings in 
infrastructure should not make the regulator handicapped in performance of its designated role. 
The Committee is constrained to note that a number of critical posts were kept vacant for years 
together. The Committee is of the view that fiscal restrictions should not be imposed 
mechanically and operational requirement of the pos t must be considered before deciding to 
abolish or keeping the post vacant. The Committee f urther feels that recruitment for filling up 
the newly created posts will be completed as per sc hedule to ease the pressure on the existing 
staff. The Committee has decided to examine the who le gamut of issue relating to DGCA 
including its authority, manpower, etc. separately. (Para 67)  
BUREAU  OF  CIVIL  AVIATION  SECURITY 
  The Committee finds that there is a major increas e in allocation of funds to BCAS under 
the plan head which clearly indicates the role of B CAS to play in the coming years. The 
Committee hopes that issues revolving around the construction of its headquarters building will 

be sorted out at the earliest. The Committee is of the opinion that introduction of biometric 
passes will strengthen the security apparatus of th e airports and will restrict the entry of 
unauthorized persons in sensitive areas.    
AERO  CLUB  OF  INDIA 
  The Committee finds that enhanced Grants-in-aid t o Aero Club of India, will be expended 
judiciously as strengthening of this institution wi ll meet the demands of qualified pilots and 
maintenance engineers for aviation industry. (Para 74)  
REGULARIZATION  OF  CASUAL  EMPLOYEES 
  It was brought to the notice of the Committee that in Jammu & Kashmir there are certain 
categories of casual employees working with NACIL a nd its predecessor Indian Airlines, Hotel 
Corporation of India and Airports Authority of India for the last so many years. They are not given the 
benefits of regular employees. They worked with the  organizations for decades together braving all 
odds in their career. The Committee, therefore, recommends that these emp loyees who worked 
with Indian Airlines/NACIL, Hotel Corporation of India and Airports Authority of India for so 
many years braving all odds may be regularized at the earliest. (Para 75)  
ROLE  OF  CIVIL  AVIATION  IN  PROMOTION  OF  TOURISM 
  The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry  of Civil Aviation can play an anchor 
role in promoting such unexplored tourist places wi th the coordination of State governments, 
tourism department and local bodies by providing re quisite airport infrastructure. Places in 
North East and Leh region could be easily accessibl e by air rather than a taxing road journey. 
The Committee feels that the Ministry should strengthen the airport infrastructure and enhance 
air services to these areas. The Committee came to know about the hardship faced by 
government employees in getting tickets under L T80  scheme for air travel using the Leave 
Travel Concession. Limited availability of seats ha s made getting confirmed tickets under this 
scheme a hard proposal. The Committee feels that NA CIL should take steps to increase the 
number of seats under the category to alleviate the present hardship of getting tickets under the 
L T80 scheme. The Committee is of the opinion that special tourist packages for air travel 
should be made available region-wise to cater the needs of air travelers.   
 
GENERAL  OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS 
  The Committee on scrutinizing of budget papers of  Ministry of Civil Aviation finds that 
the over all performance of the Ministry during the  last year has been almost satisfactory. The 
Committee feels that strengthening of aviation infrastructure, inculcating corporate governance 
in NACIL, promotion of helicopter tourism, strength ening and restructuring of DGCA and 
BCAS, empowering AAI and providing it a level playi ng field in development and 
modernization of airports, etc. are some of the major areas where the Ministry has to take some 
initiatives. Shortage of pilots, Air Traffic Contro llers, Aerodrome Inspectors, Helicopter 
inspectors is also major cause of concern. The Comm ittee feels that unless the Ministry 
addresses these issues with a sense of urgency, it cannot keep the present momentum of the 
industry for long. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry will take all the necessary 
steps to meet shortage of man power so that the mis match in demand and supply in aviation 

market is addressed success fully. The Committee further hopes that the Ministry will take more 
steps to make air travel an affordable, reliable and safe one. 
(Para 77)

INTRODUCTION  
  I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary  Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism 
and Culture, having been authorized by the Committe e to present on its behalf, do hereby present this 
One Hundred and Fifty Ninth Report on Action Taken by the Government on the 
recommendations/observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Thirty First report 
on Closure of Bangalore & Hyderabad Airports; One H undred and Forty First Report on 
Modernization of Airports and One Hundred and Forty  Second Report on Functioning of Private 
Airports.  
2.   The One Hundred Thirty First, One Hundred Fort y First and One Hundred Forty Second 
Reports of the Department-related Parliamentary Sta nding Committee on Transport, Tourism and 
Culture were presented to the Parliament on the 5th  March, 20th August and 23rd October, 2008 
respectively. 
3.   The Action Taken Replies on the recommendation s of the Committee contained in its One 
Hundred and Thirty First, One Hundred Forty First a nd One Hundred Forty Second Reports were 
received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 28th October, 2008, 2nd June  and 1st October, 
2009 respectively.  
4. The Committee in its meeting held on the 9th Feb ruary, 2010 decided that in order to have a more 
comprehensive and focused view on the Action Taken Replies furnished by the Ministry on these 
three reports, one Action Taken Report be prepared as many of the recommendations were inter-
related and pertained to the problems that needed c ommon solution. This 159th report may thus be 
treated for a comprehensive Action Taken Report by the Government on this important issue. 
5.   The Committee considered and adopted the Repor t at its meeting held on the 5th May, 2010. 
 
 
  SITARAM  YECHURY 
 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman,  
5 May , 2010 Department-related  Parliamentary Standing  
15  Vaisakha, 1932 (Saka)   Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture. 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
REPORT  
  The Report of the Committee deals with the Action  Taken by the Government on the 
observations/recommendations as contained in its 13 1st Report on the Closure of Bangalore and 
Hyderabad Airports and matters related thereto, 141 st Report on the Modernization of Airports and 
142nd Report on the Functioning of Private Airports  and the related issues on the 5th March, 20th 
August and 23rd October, 2008 respectively. 
2.   On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the C ommittee has made observations on each item of 
Action-taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry o f Civil Aviation. The recommendations of the 
Committee contained in the One Hundred and Thirty F irst, One Hundred and Forty First and One 
Hundred and Forty Second Report, action-taken there on by the Ministry and 
recommendations/observations of the Committee on ea ch item of action taken has been given in the 
succeeding paragraphs. 
CLOSURE  OF  BANGALORE  AND  HYDERABAD  AIRPORTS  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
3.  The Committee notes that the estimates and proj ections were made on the basis of the 1999 and 
2000 Statistics when the civil aviation sector was growing at 6% per annum but today it is growing at 
20% per annum. Actually, it was an underestimate of  gigantic proportions. If, the present trend 
continues in a couple of years even the present new  airports will not be able to handle the rush of 
passengers and the Government will have to look for other options. This is clear from the fact that th e 
private Greenfield airport at Bangalore is designed  to handle passenger traffic of 9 million per year.  
As noted above in 2007 itself this figure stood at 9.9million. As far as Hyderabad is concerned, the 
initial projected capacity is 7 million. In 2007 it self passenger traffic was 6.8 million. Therefore, the 
Committee recommends that the present airports shou ld be used, given the saturation of passenger 
traffic, in such a way that the private player is m aking a reasonable profit while the Government 
discharges its responsibilities of maintaining public goods and upholding public interest. 
       (Para 15) 
       (131st Report) 
4.   The Committee unanimously feels and recommends  that the existing airports at Bangalore and 
Hyderabad should not be closed for commercial operations to make the way for the commissioning of 
the private Greenfield airports. The Committee also  feels that this is the first time in the country t hat 
the Government owned airports built on the tax payers’ money are being closed for the commissioning 
of the private Greenfield airports where profit ear ning is the main motto rather than the service to t he 
passengers. This is contrary to the Government’s po licy particularly in a situation where both the 
airports are required in view of the changing scena rio in passenger traffic. This is in complete 
contravention of the ‘level playing field’ concept.  The Committee fails to understand the logic or 
rationale behind such drastic step of the Governmen t. The Committee is of the opinion that the 
Government’s reluctance to accept this Committee’s earlier unanimous recommendations presented to

USER  DEVELOPMENT  FEE  (UDF) . 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE

(142nd Report)

companies is around Rs. 330/- crores. The rest of t he finance has come from Government agencies 
and by way of debt from financial institutions. The  Committee notes that with the kind of resources 

and expertise that the Airports Authority of India has, these airports could have been easily developed 
and operated by the Airports Authority of India itself. 
(Para 31.10.4) 
(142nd Report) 
52.   The Committee is, therefore, of the view that  being leading airport infrastructure provider, the  
Airports Authority of India which has got the resou rces and expertise should have a better say in the 
modernization of airports in the country. The Commi ttee recommends that any future Greenfield 
airports or Brownfield airports project must be don e under the management of Airports Authority of 
India. JVCs can be formulated but the Airports Authority of India must have a majority holding in the 
company and management control must rest with it. 
(Para 31.10.5) 
(142nd Report) 
Reply of the Government  
53.   Approval for the Greenfield airport projects at Devanahalli and at Shamshabad were accorded 
by the Government of India, based on the proposal m ade by Governments of Andhra Pradesh and 
Karnataka. Both the State Governments want to creat e world class airports of International standard 
with world class management could be established in their respective states. 
54.  Government of India will consider the recommen dations of Parliamentary Standing Committee 
while formulating Policy for the development of future Greenfield and Brownfield airports. . 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
55.   Besides, the Airports Authority of India, adv ertently or inadvertently, appears to not being given 
its due. Even though, ATC operations of all the air ports are still with them, the closure of HAL and 
Begumpet airports and placing Airports Authority of  India virtually at the mercy of the management 
of private airports, speaks a lot about it. The man ner in which the Concession Agreement and OMDA 
were signed has also invited wide criticism and these are alleged to have violated the existing policies, 
guidelines, norms, rules, etc. The Committee feels that there appears to be some truth in the 
apprehensions that are being raised against the Gov ernment in the entire exercise of privatizing the 
airports, developing the Greenfield airports and th e related matters. The Committee expects that the 
Government of the day to provide convincing explanation to all the points, raised in this report to clear 
the apprehensions that are being flown thick and wi de. It is for the Government to clarify the entire 
matter. 
(Para 64) 
(142nd Report) 
Reply of the Government  
56.   Government of India accorded approval for the  Greenfield airport projects at Devanahalli and at 
Shamshabad, based on proposal made by Governments o f Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, for the 
creation of world class Airports with the expertise  of the private players. The world class Greenfield  
airports at Devanahalli and Shamshabad have since b een commissioned. The Government would be 
getting 4% Concession Fee in accordance with the Concession Agreements entered by Government of 
India with BIAL and GHIAL. Further, Airports Author ity of India would be getting dividend for the 

investment made in these Greenfield airports. The l and and assets of the closed HAL and Begumpet 
Airports with Airports Authority of India would be put for alternative use. 
57.   The OMDA pertains to Delhi and Mumbai airport s. The interests of AAI have been taken care 
in OMDA which amongst other things envisage provision for revenue sharing. 
FURTHER  RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
58.   The Committee finds that the replies of the Government are not convincing and feels that 
it is an attempt to mislead the Committee and natio n on privatization of airports and 
marginalizing the Airports Authority of India. The Committee is also apprehensive that the 
Government is planning to privatize majority of the  operations of the Airports Authority of 
India. The Committee still feels that the Airports Authority of India is not getting the due which 
it deserves from the Government. The Committee desires to know the policy of the Government 
in setting up of Greenfield and Brownfield airports  and the role of AAI in these new airports. 
The Committee also desires to have the detail of ch arges the private airport operators are 
paying to AAI for the services rendered to them.  
EMPLOYEES  OF  THE  AIRPORTS  AUTHORITY  OF  INDIA  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
59.  The Committee recommends that the grievances o f the employees of the both the airports should 
be well addressed by the Government. The employees should not be put into any hardship due to the 
wrong decision of the Government. The Committee fee ls that the Tripartite Committee should meet 
regularly to remove any uneasiness and settle issues agitating the employees of the Airports Authority 
of India on various issues. 
(Para 27) 
(131st Report) 
Reply of the Government  
60.   To sort out employee related issues at Delhi and Mumbai airports, Joint Working Cell during 
Operation Support Period has been set up consisting  of two representatives each of AAI and JVC of

61.   The meetings of the Tripartite Committee with  the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, 
Airports Authority of India and AAI Employees Joint  Forum are being held at regular intervals and 
various issues as stipulated in terms of reference of the Committee have been deliberated. The last 
meeting was held on 7.4.2008. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
62.   The private operators should recognize variou s staff welfare committees of Airports Authority 
of India and others working at these airports. Ther e should be regular consultative and coordination 
meeting of all the stakeholders at the new airports so as to resolve the different issues/grievances. 
(Para 16) 
(142nd Report) 
Reply of the Government  

63.   The Coordination Committee meeting of all sta keholders is being conducted on regular basis. 
An airport coordination committee has been formed s oon after commissioning the airport. The 
committee meets on the third Thursday of every month. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  OF  THE  COMMITTEE  
64.   The Government should take adequate and essen tial steps to equip the airports which are 30 to 
40 minutes flying time from the major airports to m eet any exigencies. The Committee is of the view 
that this problem can be solved if the Government expedites development/modernization of non-metro 
airports. 
(Para 42) 
(142nd Report) 
Reply of the Government  
65.   AAI has undertaken development and modernizat ion of 35 non-metro airports by providing 
world class infrastructure facilities at these airp orts. The 35 non-metro airports identified are

Bhubaneswar, Coimbatore, Patna, Port Blair, Varanas i, Agartala, Dehradun, Imphal, Ranchi, Raipur,
